name: Lisa Su
humbleBeginnings: Born in Tainan, Taiwan, in 1969, she came to the US at age 3 and grew up in Queens, where her father worked as a statistician for the city. She went to the Bronx High School of Science and earned bachelor's, master's and PhD degrees in electrical engineering at MIT.
breakthrough: After TI, 13 years at IBM (copper interconnects, the Cell processor) and a stint as CTO of Freescale, she joined AMD in 2012 and became CEO in October 2014, when it was worth about $3B. Her Zen CPUs, the all-stock Xilinx deal and Instinct AI GPUs took AMD past $1T in value. In 2025 she signed a 6-gigawatt GPU deal with OpenAI.
shieldingStrategy: A hired CEO with no founder stake. Her billionaire status comes from AMD stock awards granted near the company's low point that then compounded. Her wealth is held as listed AMD shares and options, with no dual-class or family-holding structure.

breakthroughDetail.d: Wrote her MIT PhD on silicon-on-insulator transistors. At IBM she worked on copper interconnect technology and the Cell processor with Sony and Toshiba.
She became CEO in October 2014, when AMD's market cap was about $3B. The Zen architecture (2017) began the recovery, and AMD passed Intel in market value in 2022.
Announced in October 2020 and closed February 14, 2022 as an all-stock deal. She added the chair title in 2022.

In October 2025 OpenAI agreed to deploy 6GW of AMD GPUs, starting with MI450. AMD gave it a warrant for up to 160M shares at $0.01 that vests with purchase and stock-price milestones, about 10% of AMD if fully exercised.

shieldingDetail.d: She topped the AP's 2020 CEO pay survey, the first woman to do so. Most of that pay was AMD stock granted when the shares were cheap.
Her fortune is AMD shares she holds directly, with no super-voting class or private holding company.
Su and Jensen Huang are first cousins once removed through Huang's mother. Su said they did not grow up together and first met at an industry event.

sources.label: Yahoo Finance / Business Insider — Su on her distant cousin Jensen Huang (Dec 2024)
Tom's Hardware — OpenAI signs 6GW AMD GPU deal

name: Satya Nadella
humbleBeginnings: Born in Hyderabad in 1967, the son of an Indian Administrative Service officer. He studied electrical engineering at Manipal, came to the US for an MS in computer science at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee and worked at Sun Microsystems before joining Microsoft in 1992.
breakthrough: As president of Server and Tools he built the cloud business that became Azure. He succeeded Steve Ballmer as CEO in February 2014 and became chairman in 2021. He bought LinkedIn and GitHub, and from 2019 he made Microsoft OpenAI's main backer, ending a decade of stagnant stock and making Microsoft one of the most valuable companies in the world.
shieldingStrategy: A hired CEO. Forbes says he owns about 0.01% of Microsoft, and that stake plus more than $700M of past share sales make him a billionaire. His pay is mostly performance stock.

breakthroughDetail.d: Led the Server and Tools business and its shift to cloud infrastructure before becoming Microsoft's third CEO on February 4, 2014.
Mojang/Minecraft ($2.5B, 2014), LinkedIn ($26.2B, 2016) and GitHub ($7.5B, 2018).

Microsoft invested $1B in 2019, $2B in 2022 and committed $10B in January 2023. When OpenAI's board fired Sam Altman in November 2023, Nadella offered Altman and Greg Brockman a new Microsoft AI team, which helped bring Altman back. Microsoft took about 27% of OpenAI Group PBC in the October 2025 recapitalization.
In November 2025 Microsoft and Nvidia committed about $15B combined to Anthropic (Microsoft up to $5B), and Anthropic committed to $30B of Azure compute.

shieldingDetail.d: His 2024 compensation totaled $79.1M, mostly stock awards.
Forbes credits his billionaire status to his small Microsoft stake plus over $700M in prior share sales.
He holds stakes in Seattle Sounders FC and the Seattle Orcas cricket team.

name: Sundar Pichai
humbleBeginnings: Born in Tamil Nadu in 1972 and raised in Chennai in a modest household. His father was an electrical engineer at GEC and his mother a stenographer. Forbes reports his father spent a year's salary on his plane ticket to Stanford in 1993.
breakthrough: After IIT Kharagpur, a Stanford MS, Applied Materials, McKinsey and a Wharton MBA, he joined Google in 2004. He led Chrome, ChromeOS and Android, became Google CEO in October 2015 and Alphabet CEO in December 2019, and pushed Google toward AI with Gemini.
shieldingStrategy: A hired CEO who holds about 0.02% of Alphabet. He holds no super-voting control, since the founders' Class B shares keep that. His wealth is triennial performance-stock grants, and he has sold over $500M of shares before tax.

breakthroughDetail.d: Joined in 2004, reportedly interviewing the day Gmail launched. He led product development for Chrome, ChromeOS and Drive, then took over Android.

Google's annual payments to Apple for default search on Safari were central to the DOJ antitrust trial. The September 2025 remedy ruling let the payments continue but barred exclusive search contracts.
On January 12, 2026 Google and Apple announced a multi-year deal under which Apple's next foundation models will be based on Gemini models and Google cloud technology.
Under him Google invested $500M plus a $1.5B commitment in Anthropic (October 2023) and $1B more in March 2025. In October 2025 it gave Anthropic access to up to one million TPUs.

shieldingDetail.d: His pay is lumpy because of performance-based stock awards granted every three years. It topped $200M in 2022.
Alphabet's Class B shares (10 votes each) keep Page and Brin in control, so his small Class C/A stake is purely economic.
Forbes reports over $500M in pre-tax share sales.

sources.label: Google — Joint statement from Google and Apple (Jan 12, 2026)
Wikipedia — United States v. Google LLC (2020)

name: Andy Jassy
wealthNote: Not on Forbes' billionaire list. SEC Form 4 data compiled by InsiderTrades shows 2,235,766 Amazon shares worth about $562M as of August 21, 2026. Adding cash from years of quarterly sales and unvested awards from his 2021 ten-year package (about $212.7M), he sits in the $500M–$1B tier.
humbleBeginnings: Grew up in Scarsdale, New York, the son of Everett Jassy, a senior partner at the law firm Dewey Ballantine. He graduated cum laude from Harvard, where he ran advertising for The Harvard Crimson, and then earned a Harvard MBA.
breakthrough: He joined Amazon in 1997 as a marketing manager and later became Jeff Bezos's technical adviser, or 'shadow'. In 2003 he co-conceived Amazon Web Services, which launched in 2006 and became Amazon's profit engine. He ran AWS (CEO from 2016) and succeeded Bezos as Amazon CEO on July 5, 2021.
shieldingStrategy: A career employee whose wealth is Amazon RSUs. He sells small blocks of stock on a regular quarterly schedule rather than in large discretionary sales.

breakthroughDetail.d: Served as Jeff Bezos's technical adviser before co-conceiving AWS in 2003.
AWS launched in 2006, and he led it until he became Amazon CEO in 2021.
Amazon invested $1.25B in Anthropic in September 2023, $2.75B in March 2024 and $4B in November 2024, for $8B in total.

AWS signed a $38B, seven-year compute deal with OpenAI in November 2025. On March 2, 2026 Amazon said it would invest $50B in OpenAI ($15B up front, $35B on conditions) and expand the cloud deal by $100B over 8 years, including about 2GW of Trainium capacity.

shieldingDetail.d: His 2021 CEO package was a ten-year stock award valued at about $212.7M, which keeps most of his pay tied to Amazon's share price.
Form 4 filings show regular quarterly sales of roughly 20,000–50,000 shares, such as 20,000 shares at about $259 on August 21, 2026.

sources.label: AWS Blog — Weekly roundup: OpenAI partnership (Mar 2, 2026)

name: Steve Ballmer
humbleBeginnings: Born in Detroit in 1956, the son of a Ford operations manager. He was valedictorian at Detroit Country Day and studied applied math and economics at Harvard, where he lived down the hall from Bill Gates. He worked two years at Procter & Gamble and enrolled at Stanford's business school.
breakthrough: In 1980 he left Stanford to join Microsoft as employee #30 and Gates's first business manager, on a $50,000 salary plus profit-sharing. He owned 8% when the company incorporated in 1981. He was president from 1998 and CEO from 2000 to 2014, then bought the LA Clippers for $2B. Because he kept most of his Microsoft stock (about 4%), he is now one of the ten richest people in the world.
shieldingStrategy: He never diversified: Bloomberg says more than 90% of his net worth is Microsoft stock, and he calls himself its largest individual shareholder. He gives through Ballmer Group, an LLC rather than a private foundation, and has not signed the Giving Pledge.

breakthroughDetail.d: Gates hired him in 1980 as business manager. Equity from the profit-sharing deal gave him 8% at the 1981 incorporation.

Named CEO on January 13, 2000. Sales tripled and profits doubled, but the stock stagnated and Microsoft missed mobile. He retired as CEO on February 4, 2014 (succeeded by Satya Nadella) and left the board in August 2014.

He bought the Clippers for $2B in 2014, and Forbes now values the team at $7.5B. He privately financed the roughly $2B Intuit Dome (opened August 2024) through Murphy's Bowl LLC, after buying The Forum for $400M in 2020 to clear litigation.

shieldingDetail.d: He holds about 4% of Microsoft directly, and per Bloomberg more than 90% of his wealth is Microsoft stock. That concentration is what lifted him past Gates in the rankings.

Ballmer Group (2015, with wife Connie) is an LLC, not a foundation, so it can fund advocacy and is not subject to foundation payout rules. Forbes says the couple has given over $7.4B since 2014. He has not signed the Giving Pledge.

On September 2, 2026 the NBA ended its Kawhi Leonard/Aspiration investigation. It fined the Clippers $30M, took five first-round picks (2029–33) and suspended Ballmer for one year. The Clippers dispute the findings.

sources.label: Fox Business — Ballmer tops Bill Gates' wealth (Jul 2024)
NBA.com — Penalties from investigation of LA Clippers and Kawhi Leonard

name: Michael Bloomberg
humbleBeginnings: Born in Boston in 1942 and raised in Medford, Massachusetts. His father was a bookkeeper for a dairy company who never earned more than about $6,000 a year. He studied engineering at Johns Hopkins and earned an MBA at Harvard.
breakthrough: He joined Salomon Brothers in 1966 at $9,000 a year and became a general partner running equity trading and systems. When Salomon merged with Phibro in 1981 he was pushed out with about $10M for his equity, and used it to found Innovative Market Systems, later Bloomberg L.P. Merrill Lynch was its first customer and bought 30% for $30M.
shieldingStrategy: Bloomberg L.P. has never gone public and is not on the Fortune 500. He owns about 88% of it, having bought Merrill Lynch's 30% back in two steps (1996 and 2008). He has pledged his stake to Bloomberg Philanthropies, which gives away billions a year.

breakthroughDetail.d: He joined Salomon Brothers in 1966, became a general partner in 1972 and ran equity trading and systems development. When Phibro acquired Salomon in 1981 he received about $10M for his equity and left.

He co-founded Innovative Market Systems in 1981 with Thomas Secunda, Duncan MacMillan and Charles Zegar. The Market Master terminal shipped in December 1982, and the firm was renamed Bloomberg L.P. in 1986.
Merrill Lynch bought 20 terminals in 1982 and a 30% stake for $30M, with a five-year restriction on selling to rivals that was lifted in 1984.
Bloomberg L.P. had about $15B of revenue and 26,000 employees in 2024. He was CEO from 1981 to 2001 and again from 2014 to 2023.

shieldingDetail.d: In 1996 he repurchased a third of Merrill's stake for $200M, valuing the firm at $2B. In 2008 he bought Merrill's remaining 20% for about $4.4B, leaving him with about 88%.
Bloomberg L.P. is privately held and does not appear on the Fortune 500, so it publishes no public financial statements.
He signed the Giving Pledge in 2010, and Forbes reports he has committed his Bloomberg L.P. stake to Bloomberg Philanthropies. He gave $4.3B in 2025 alone.
In 2023 he named Vlad Kliatchko CEO and Mark Carney non-executive chair, while keeping ownership.

sources.label: NBC News — $1B Bloomberg gift to Johns Hopkins (2024)

name: Ken Griffin
humbleBeginnings: Born in 1968 in Daytona Beach, Florida. As a Harvard economics student he put a satellite dish on his dorm roof to get live quotes and traded convertible bonds with about $100,000 raised from his grandmother and others.
breakthrough: Chicago fund-of-funds manager Frank Meyer of Glenwood Capital gave him $1M to trade, and in 1990 he founded Citadel with $4.6M. Citadel became one of the most profitable hedge funds ever, and its sister firm Citadel Securities (2002) grew into the largest U.S. retail market maker, handling about one in four U.S. stock trades.
shieldingStrategy: He owns about 80–85% of Citadel and is majority owner of Citadel Securities, both private partnerships. In 2022 he sold a minority stake in Citadel Securities to Sequoia and Paradigm for $1.15B, which set a $22B valuation without an IPO. He moved both firms' headquarters from Chicago to Miami in 2022.

breakthroughDetail.d: He began trading convertible bonds from his Harvard dorm in 1987, three years before founding Citadel, using a rooftop satellite dish for real-time prices.
Frank Meyer of Glenwood Capital Investments allocated $1M for him to trade. Citadel launched in 1990 with $4.6M and had about $77B under management by 2026.

Citadel Securities pays retail brokers for their order flow. Fourth-quarter 2020 Rule 606 reports showed it paying nine brokers, including Robinhood, TD Ameritrade, Schwab, E*Trade, Fidelity and Ally Invest. It was the top venue for stock and option orders at most of them.

In November 2007 Citadel put about $2.5B into E*Trade for its mortgage-securities portfolio, 19.99% of the stock and a board seat. In January 2021 Citadel and Point72 put $2.75B into Melvin Capital after its GameStop short losses, about $2B of it from Citadel.

shieldingDetail.d: Citadel LLC and Citadel Securities are separate private firms, both majority-owned by Griffin. Neither publishes financial statements the way a listed company must.
Sequoia Capital and Paradigm invested $1.15B in Citadel Securities in January 2022 at about a $22B valuation, which priced his stake without a public listing.
In June 2022 he moved Citadel's headquarters from Chicago to Miami.

He gave Harvard $300M in 2023, and its graduate school of arts and sciences now bears his name. In September 2026 he pledged $3B to Carnegie Mellon, including $2B for a new Miami campus, the largest gift in higher-education history.

sources.label: Wall Street on Parade — Citadel pays for order flow from nine brokers

name: Dan Gilbert
humbleBeginnings: Born in Detroit in 1962. His father owned a bar, Sakesy's, and his grandfather managed a car wash. Forbes says he started his mortgage firm at 22 with $5,000 he had made selling pizzas, while studying for a law degree at Wayne State after Michigan State.
breakthrough: In 1985 he co-founded Rock Financial with his brother Gary and others, and it became an early online mortgage lender. He sold it to Intuit in 1999, bought it back as Quicken Loans in 2002, and built it into Rocket Mortgage, the largest U.S. mortgage lender. Rocket Companies went public in 2020, and in 2025 it agreed to buy Redfin ($1.75B) and Mr. Cooper ($9.4B).
shieldingStrategy: He sold his company at the top of the dot-com boom for Intuit stock (about $532M), then bought the mortgage business back in 2002 for a small fraction of that price. After the 2020 IPO he kept control through Rock Holdings, which held about 93% of Rocket Companies' voting power, so only a sliver of the company was floated.

breakthroughDetail.d: He co-founded it with Ron Berman, Lindsay Gross and his brother Gary Gilbert, and it became one of the first lenders to take mortgage applications online in the late 1990s.
Intuit bought Rock Financial in 1999 for about $532M in stock and renamed it Quicken Loans. In 2002 Gilbert's investor group bought it back for about $64M and kept the Quicken name.
Rocket Companies raised about $1.8B in its August 2020 IPO. In 2025 it agreed to buy Redfin and Mr. Cooper, adding a home-search site and mortgage servicing.
He bought the Cleveland Cavaliers for $375M in 2005, then an NBA record. His Rock Gaming opened Horseshoe Cleveland in 2012 with Caesars Entertainment and bought out Caesars' 20% stake in 2015.

shieldingDetail.d: Rock Holdings held about 93% of Rocket Companies, and Gilbert controlled 79% of the shares at the 2020 IPO, according to Wikipedia.
He took Intuit stock at the 1999 peak and bought the business back in 2002 for about $64M, roughly an eighth of the earlier price.
Bedrock bought more than 100 downtown Detroit properties, and Wikipedia says it had invested about $7.5B there by 2026.
He and his then-wife Jennifer signed the Giving Pledge in 2012. Much of their giving funds neurofibromatosis research.

sources.label: Fox Sports — Buffett, Gilbert offer $1 billion for perfect bracket

name: Stuart Miller
humbleBeginnings: Born in 1957 into the business: his father Leonard Miller co-founded Lennar in Miami in 1954 with Arnold Rosen. Forbes says Stuart started on the company's lawn crew at 12. He graduated from Harvard in 1979 and University of Miami law school in 1982, then joined Lennar.
breakthrough: He became CEO in 1997 and turned a Florida builder into the largest U.S. homebuilder through acquisitions: U.S. Home ($476M, 2000), WCI ($643M, 2017) and CalAtlantic (about $9.3B, 2018). He moved to executive chairman in 2018 and took sole charge as executive chairman and CEO when co-CEO Jon Jaffe retired at the end of 2025.
shieldingStrategy: Lennar has two share classes, and its Class B shares carry ten votes each. Miller held about 69% of the Class B shares and roughly 40% of the combined votes in the 2025 proxy, which gives him effective control with a minority of the equity. He has also moved assets off Lennar's books, spinning off Millrose Properties as a land-option platform in 2025 and selling apartment portfolios.

breakthroughDetail.d: Leonard Miller and Arnold Rosen founded Lennar, whose name combines their first names, in 1954. It went public in 1971 and listed on the NYSE in 1972.
As CEO from 1997 to 2018 he bought U.S. Home in 2000 for $476M in cash and stock, and WCI Communities in 2017 for $643M.
The roughly $9.3B CalAtlantic merger, completed in February 2018, made Lennar the largest U.S. homebuilder, with more than $17B of combined revenue.
In June 2024 Lennar's Quarterra division sold KKR about 5,200 apartments for $2.1B. In February 2025 Lennar spun off Millrose Properties to hold homesites under option.

shieldingDetail.d: Each Class B share has ten votes. His roughly 69% of Class B gave him about 40% of total votes in the 2025 proxy, held partly through trusts and family charitable foundations.
Millrose buys land and sells homesites to Lennar under option contracts, so Lennar holds less land directly. Miller also holds a significant but non-majority share of Millrose's votes.
Forbes says he co-founded East Rock, a family office that invests in distressed assets.
He chairs the UHealth (University of Miami Health System) board. The university's medical school is named for his father.

sources.label: CRE Daily — KKR buys $2.1B Quarterra portfolio

name: Charles Koch
humbleBeginnings: Born in Wichita in 1935, the son of Fred C. Koch, an engineer who built an oil-refining business. He was not a self-made founder: he earned three MIT engineering degrees (1957–59) and joined his father's Rock Island Oil & Refining in 1961.
breakthrough: He became president in 1967 after his father's death and renamed the company Koch Industries in his honor. Using a philosophy he calls Market-Based Management, he expanded from refining into pipelines, chemicals, paper (Georgia-Pacific, $21B, 2005), electronics (Molex, $7.2B, 2013), glass (Guardian) and software (Infor, 2017–2020). Revenue reached about $125B, and in 2024 the company renamed itself Koch, Inc.
shieldingStrategy: Koch, Inc. has stayed private, and it is the second-largest U.S. private company after Cargill. In 1983 Charles and David Koch bought out their brothers Frederick and Bill, and since then the two branches have each held about 42% of the voting stock. Between 2020 and 2022 he moved about $5.3B of nonvoting stock to two nonprofits while keeping his 42% voting control.

breakthroughDetail.d: He joined Rock Island Oil & Refining in 1961, became president in 1967 and renamed it Koch Industries. Wikipedia says that by 2006 revenue had compounded about 18% a year to $90B.
Koch completed its $21B purchase of the NYSE-listed tissue, paper and building-products maker in December 2005, paying about $48 a share.

Koch bought connector maker Molex for $7.2B in 2013. It took two-thirds of enterprise-software firm Infor for $2.68B in 2017 and bought the rest from Golden Gate Capital in 2020, at an $11B valuation.

breakthroughDetail.t: Running Infor on its own operations.
breakthroughDetail.d: After Infor came in under budget on a Georgia-Pacific project, Koch put four directors on Infor's board and rolled out Infor CloudSuite, which runs on AWS, to its 120,000 employees.

shieldingDetail.d: Koch, Inc. remains private, so its acquisitions are funded largely from retained earnings and debt, without public shareholders.
After the 1983 buyout of Frederick and Bill, Charles and David each held about 42%. David's stake went to his widow Julia and her family after his death in 2019.

Between 2020 and 2022 he transferred about $5.3B of nonvoting Koch stock to two nonprofits that have fewer limits on political activity than private foundations. Forbes says his 42% voting stake was unchanged.
In 2023 Koch, Inc. named its first-ever co-CEO, while Charles remained chairman and CEO.

sources.label: SiliconANGLE — Koch 'pushes' Infor in global CloudSuite implementation

name: Michael Jordan
humbleBeginnings: Born in Brooklyn in 1963 and raised in Wilmington, North Carolina, where his mother worked at a bank and his father was an equipment supervisor. Across a 15-year NBA career he earned only about $90M in salary.
breakthrough: In 1984 Nike signed him to a deal that paid royalties on products carrying his name, then unheard of for an athlete. Air Jordan grew into Jordan Brand, which brought Nike $5.1B in 2022, and Forbes says Nike now pays him nearly $300M a year. In 2010 he bought control of the Charlotte Bobcats from Robert L. Johnson for $275M and sold it in 2023 at a $3B valuation.
shieldingStrategy: His fortune rests on a royalty contract rather than a salary, so Nike carries the manufacturing and marketing risk while he collects a share of sales. He sold his majority of the Hornets but kept a minority stake, and he directs giving through a $100M, 10-year pledge made with Jordan Brand.

breakthroughDetail.d: Wikipedia: Jordan signed with Nike on Oct 26, 1984 for $2.5M, 'three times more than any other deal' in the NBA, and 'would get royalties from products sold by Nike with his name'.
Jordan and Nike launched Jordan Brand as a subsidiary in 1997. In 2022 it brought in $5.1B, with a reported $150–256M going to Jordan; Forbes now puts his Nike royalties near $300M a year.

He bought a minority stake in the Bobcats in 2006 and ran basketball operations, then paid Robert L. Johnson $275M for control in 2010, becoming the first former NBA player to own a majority of a team.
In 2023 he sold his majority to Gabe Plotkin and Rick Schnall at about a $3B valuation. The NBA approved it 29–1 on July 24, 2023.

shieldingDetail.d: He owns no stake in Nike; his income is a contractual share of Jordan-branded sales, which needs no capital from him and scales with the brand.

shieldingDetail.t: Kept a seat at the table.
shieldingDetail.d: After the 2023 sale he retained a minority stake in the Hornets, keeping exposure to franchise appreciation without control.
Forbes lists a 2020 investment and advisory role at DraftKings and co-ownership of NASCAR's 23XI Racing (since 2020).
In June 2020 Jordan and Jordan Brand pledged $100M over 10 years to groups working on racial equality, social justice and access to education, $50M from each.

sources.label: CBS News — NBA approves Jordan's sale of the Hornets
Nike — Jordan Brand statement on commitment to the Black community

name: Dr. Dre (Andre Young)
humbleBeginnings: Born Andre Romell Young in Compton in 1965 and raised partly by his grandmother in the New Wilmington Arms housing project after his parents divorced. He started out as a club DJ before co-founding N.W.A in 1987.
breakthrough: After Death Row he founded Aftermath Entertainment under Interscope in 1996 and signed Eminem (1998), 50 Cent (2002) and Kendrick Lamar. In 2006 he co-founded Beats with Interscope chief Jimmy Iovine, and Apple bought it in 2014 for $3B in cash and stock.
shieldingStrategy: He took equity in Beats rather than an endorsement fee, so the Apple sale turned the brand into cash and Apple stock. His label sits inside Interscope's distribution system, and part of his Apple payout vested over time as a retention package.

breakthroughDetail.d: He co-founded Death Row with Suge Knight in 1991, left in March 1996 and 'formed his own label, Aftermath Entertainment', distributed by Interscope.
Aftermath signed Eminem in 1998 and 50 Cent in 2002, and later Kendrick Lamar. Forbes ranks the label as his first fortune engine.
Co-founded with Jimmy Iovine in 2006; headphones launched in 2008. HTC bought 50.1% for $309M in 2010, and Carlyle invested $500M at a $1B valuation in 2013.
On May 28, 2014 Apple agreed to buy Beats for $3B ($2.6B plus about $400M vesting over time). The deal closed in August 2014 and Dre joined Apple as an employee.

shieldingDetail.d: As a co-founder, he held Beats equity rather than a licensing fee, so the brand's value came to him when Apple bought it.
About $400M of Apple's price vested over time, tying the founders' payout to staying on at Apple.
In 2013 he and Iovine gave $70M to USC for the Jimmy Iovine and Andre Young Academy.
In 2024 he and Snoop Dogg launched Gin & Juice by Dre and Snoop, a ready-to-drink brand, per Forbes.

name: Jimmy Iovine
humbleBeginnings: Born in 1953 in Red Hook, Brooklyn, the son of a longshoreman. He dropped out of John Jay College at 19 and started out cleaning a recording studio before becoming an engineer for John Lennon and Bruce Springsteen.
breakthrough: After producing records for Patti Smith and others, he co-founded Interscope with Ted Field in 1989–90 as a $20M joint venture with Atlantic. Interscope distributed Death Row and Aftermath, and MCA (later Universal) bought half of it in 1996 for about $200M. With Dr. Dre he co-founded Beats in 2006, sold it to Apple for $3B in 2014, and then led the launch of Apple Music.
shieldingStrategy: He sold Interscope in stages, half to MCA in 1996 after buying back Time Warner's half, and stayed on to run it inside Universal. He held Beats equity through outside rounds and the Apple sale. Since leaving Apple in 2018 he has invested as a private backer.

breakthroughDetail.d: He worked with John Lennon and Bruce Springsteen in the early 1970s and broke through producing Patti Smith's Easter (1978).
Founded with Ted Field as a '$20 million joint venture' with Atlantic that gave artists 'full creative control'. In 1992 it took on distribution of Death Row Records.
Under pressure over gangsta rap, Time Warner sold its 50% back to Field and Iovine for $115M in 1995. MCA bought 50% for a reported $200M in 1996, and in 1999 Interscope absorbed Geffen and A&M.

He co-founded Beats with Dr. Dre in 2006 and sold it to Apple for $3B in 2014. Beats Music became Apple Music (launched June 30, 2015), which passed 50M subscribers by May 2018. He left Apple in August 2018.

shieldingDetail.d: He turned his Interscope stake into cash in steps, buying out Time Warner in 1995 and then selling half to MCA in 1996, while staying on as chairman.
Beats took in HTC ($309M for 50.1% in 2010, later sold back) and Carlyle ($500M in 2013) before Apple. The founders kept their stakes throughout.
About $400M of Apple's purchase price vested over time for Beats' leaders.
He and Dre gave USC $70M in 2013. Forbes lists later investments in 88rising, NTWRK and the Professional Fighters League.

name: David Steward
humbleBeginnings: Born in Chicago in 1951 and raised in segregated Clinton, Missouri, one of eight children of a father who held several manual-labor jobs. In 1967 he took part in integrating the town's public pool.
breakthrough: After sales jobs at Missouri Pacific Railroad and FedEx, where he was salesman of the year, he founded World Wide Technology in 1990 with Jim Kavanaugh as an equipment reseller. WWT became Cisco's largest partner and Dell's first Titanium Black partner, and it now has about $20B in annual revenue, making it the largest Black-owned company in the U.S.
shieldingStrategy: WWT is privately held, so his ownership is not marked to a public share price and the company does not have to publish its results. He gives through the Steward Family Foundation, set up with his wife Thelma.

breakthroughDetail.d: He sold for Missouri Pacific Railroad (1975–79) and FedEx (1979–84), where he was salesman of the year and entered its sales hall of fame in 1981. He then owned Transportation Business Specialists and Transport Administrative Services.

WWT's site says the Cisco partnership began more than 30 years ago and WWT is now 'Cisco's largest and most strategic global partner with more than $6B in Cisco sales'. It was also Dell's 'first-ever Titanium Black partner'.

WWT is an Elite Nvidia partner and in March 2025 was named Nvidia's Americas Enterprise Partner of the Year for the seventh year running. In December 2023 it committed $500M over three years to AI, including its AI Proving Ground lab.
Revenue passed $1B by 2003, was $4.1B in 2010 (No. 1 on the BE100s) and is now about $20B, with over 14,000 employees. In 2025 it bought Softchoice for $1.3B.

shieldingDetail.d: WWT has never listed, so Steward and Kavanaugh keep control and do not publish financial results the way a public company must.
WWT resells and integrates products from more than 100 technology firms, which spreads its dependence across many vendors.
The Steward Family Foundation backs education, health and human services. In 2018 he gave $1.3M to found the David and Thelma Steward Institute for Jazz Studies at UMSL.

sources.label: WWT — Dell Technologies 2023 North America Partner of the Year
WWT — Nvidia 2025 Americas Enterprise Partner of the Year
Black Enterprise — UBR Spotlight: David Steward

name: Ursula Burns
wealthNote: No credible published net worth exists, and the billion-dollar figures on content sites are unsupported. The estimate rests on her reported Xerox pay: about $9.9M in 2009, $10.6M in 2010, $22.2M in 2014 and $10.6M in 2015, mostly in stock that fell sharply in value. Board fees come on top.
humbleBeginnings: Born in 1958 to Panamanian immigrants and raised by a single mother in the Baruch Houses, a housing project on Manhattan's Lower East Side. She studied mechanical engineering at Brooklyn Poly (1980), then earned a master's at Columbia (1981).
breakthrough: She joined Xerox as a summer engineering intern in 1980 and rose through its business units to president in 2007 and CEO in July 2009. That made her the first Black woman to lead a Fortune 500 company. She bought Affiliated Computer Services for $6.4B to move Xerox into services, then split the company in 2016–17, spinning that business off as Conduent.
shieldingStrategy: Like most hired CEOs, she built wealth through salary and stock awards rather than founder equity. Since leaving Xerox she has spread her income across board seats at American Express, ExxonMobil and Uber and roles such as chairing and running VEON.

breakthroughDetail.d: She started at Xerox in 1980 in engineering roles. From 1992 to 2000 she ran a series of business units, including Office Color and Facsimile, and became president in 2007 and CEO in 2009, succeeding Anne Mulcahy.
She bought Affiliated Computer Services for $6.4B (2009–10) to shift Xerox from copiers toward business-process outsourcing.
With activist Carl Icahn pressing for change, Xerox spun its ACS-based services arm off as Conduent. She stepped down as CEO at the end of 2016.
She led the White House STEM program (2009–16) and chaired the President's Export Council (2015–16).

shieldingDetail.d: In 2015, $8M of her $10.6M package was stock awards (2014: $15.5M of $22.2M), so her wealth tracked Xerox's share price.
Ken Chenault brought her onto American Express's board in January 2004. She was elected to ExxonMobil's board in 2012 and also sat on Uber's.
She was chair and CEO of VEON from 2018 to 2020, moving her income from a single employer to several boards and roles.

sources.label: American Express 8-K — Burns elected to board (Jan 2004)

name: Ken Chenault
wealthNote: Based on an Equilar analysis cited by the FT: about $370M in pay over 17 years as CEO ($150M options, $104M shares, $24M salary, $76M bonuses). The figure is pre-tax and excludes pre-2006 vested awards. Add later General Catalyst and board pay.
humbleBeginnings: Born in 1951 and raised on Long Island; his father was a dentist and his mother a dental hygienist. He studied history at Bowdoin (1973) and law at Harvard (1976), then worked as a lawyer at Rogers & Wells and a consultant at Bain.
breakthrough: He joined American Express as director of strategic planning in 1981 and became president in 1997 and CEO in 2001, a post he held for 17 years. He was the third Black CEO of a Fortune 500 company. During the 2008 crisis he turned AmEx into a bank holding company, which made it eligible for TARP funds.
shieldingStrategy: His wealth came from stock options and shares in a company whose largest long-term holder is Berkshire Hathaway. Since 2018 he has spread it across a venture firm, General Catalyst, as chairman and managing director, and board seats at Airbnb and Berkshire itself.

breakthroughDetail.d: He joined AmEx in 1981, became president and COO in 1997 and was CEO from January 2001 to February 2018 and chairman from April 2001.
In November 2008 AmEx became a bank holding company with Federal Reserve approval, which made it eligible for TARP.
In 2016 Costco's U.S. card deal moved to Citi and Visa, ending AmEx's exclusive deal there.
Since February 2018 he has been chairman and a managing director of General Catalyst, an early backer of Airbnb and Stripe.

shieldingDetail.d: Of his roughly $370M in CEO pay, about $254M came in options and shares, per Equilar and the FT.

Berkshire's 2026 proxy says he has been a Berkshire director since 2020 and is an Airbnb director (since 2018). He was earlier on the boards of Facebook (2018–20), IBM (1998–2019) and Procter & Gamble (2008–19).
AmEx paid his 2017 incentive (~$8.3M) in RSUs vesting a year after he retired, and pays him a $300K yearly office stipend for nine years.

In 2020 he co-founded OneTen with Ken Frazier and others to hire and promote one million Black Americans over 10 years. He chairs the advisory council of the Smithsonian's African American history museum.

sources.label: PYMNTS — AmEx CEO to have earned $370M
STAT — Ken Frazier's General Catalyst role

name: Ken Frazier
wealthNote: Based on Equilar's count of $201.3M in pay he actually received at Merck from 2011 to 2019, plus $22.1M reported for 2020, before taxes. In 2017 he held about 600,000 Merck shares (~$37M). No Forbes or Bloomberg figure exists.
humbleBeginnings: Born in 1954 in North Philadelphia, where his father Otis worked as a janitor. He studied at Penn State and Harvard Law (1978), then became a partner at Drinker Biddle & Reath. In 1991 he took on a pro bono death-row case that ended in the client's acquittal.
breakthrough: He joined Merck in 1992 and, as general counsel, ran its defense against the Vioxx lawsuits, which settled in 2007 for $4.85B. As CEO from 2011, the first Black CEO of a major pharmaceutical company, he bet Merck on Keytruda (approved 2014), which made the company one of the world's largest cancer-drug makers. He spun off Organon in 2021.
shieldingStrategy: As a hired CEO, his wealth came from Merck shares and options, which he held through Keytruda's rise. He stayed on as executive chairman after 2021 and moved into venture capital as chairman of General Catalyst's $600M Health Assurance initiative.

breakthroughDetail.d: He was a partner at Drinker Biddle & Reath. His pro bono client James 'Bo' Cochran had his conviction overturned in 1995 and was acquitted at retrial in 1997.
As Merck's general counsel he became widely known for leading the defense against the Vioxx lawsuits; the remaining cases settled in 2007 for $4.85B.
As CEO (2011–21) he focused Merck on Keytruda, approved in 2014, which was the world's best-selling drug in 2023 and brought in $29.5B in 2024.
Merck spun off Organon in 2021, and Robert Davis succeeded him as CEO that year.

shieldingDetail.d: His 2020 package of $22.1M included $10.8M in stock and $4.7M in options.
After stepping down in June 2021 he remained executive chairman of Merck.
In July 2021 General Catalyst named him to lead its health assurance initiatives, including a $600M Health Assurance Fund.

He was an ExxonMobil director from 2009 and its lead director from 2020. He co-chairs OneTen, which he co-founded with Ken Chenault in December 2020. In 2017 he resigned from Trump's manufacturing council after Charlottesville.

sources.label: Equilar — Merck CEO realized over $200M during tenure
STAT — Ken Frazier steps out in new venture capital role
The Conference Board — Kenneth C. Frazier

name: Jamie Dimon
humbleBeginnings: Born in New York City in 1956 into a Greek-American family of stockbrokers: his grandfather, a Greek immigrant who had banked in Smyrna and Athens, and his father both worked at Shearson. He graduated summa cum laude from Tufts in 1978 and took a Harvard MBA as a Baker Scholar in 1982.
breakthrough: Sandy Weill recruited him to American Express in 1982. He followed Weill out in 1985, became CFO of Commercial Credit at 30 and helped build it, through mergers, into Citigroup (1998), before Weill asked him to resign that November. He became CEO of Bank One in 2000, merged it into JPMorgan Chase in 2004 and has been CEO since December 31, 2005 and chairman since December 31, 2006.
shieldingStrategy: A hired executive, not a founder: his fortune is JPMorgan stock earned as pay. Much of it sits in family trusts and an LLC, and in 2024 he began selling for what the bank called diversification and tax planning. A 2021 board award of 1.5M stock appreciation rights ties him to the bank until 2031.

breakthroughDetail.d: Weill hired him as his assistant at American Express after Harvard. Dimon turned down offers from Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and Lehman Brothers. Their Commercial Credit (1986) roll-up became Citigroup on October 8, 1998, and Dimon left that November.
Bank One brought in the former Citigroup executive as CEO in 2000. It merged with JPMorgan Chase on July 1, 2004, and Dimon became president and COO, then CEO.

In March 2008 JPMorgan agreed to buy Bear Stearns for $2 a share, later raised to $10 (about $1.2B), with a $29B New York Fed loan through Maiden Lane LLC. It bought Washington Mutual's banking operations from the FDIC for $1.836B in September 2008 and most of First Republic's assets in May 2023 for a $10.6B payment to the FDIC.
JPMorgan, Amazon and Berkshire Hathaway launched the Haven health venture for their U.S. employees in January 2018. It shut down at the end of February 2021.

shieldingDetail.d: Forbes says he became a billionaire mainly through his JPMorgan stake. JPMorgan requires him to hold at least 1 million shares; Fortune reported family holdings of about 8.6 million shares in 2024.
In February 2024 he sold about $150M of stock at $182.73 a share, the first sale under a plan the bank said was for financial diversification and tax planning.
On July 20, 2021, the board granted 1,500,000 stock appreciation rights, exercisable no earlier than July 20, 2026. Net shares must be held until July 20, 2031.
The James and Judith K. Dimon Foundation gave $12M to 12 HBCUs through UNCF in August 2026.

sources.label: SEC — JPMorgan Chase 8-K, July 2021 special award
Fortune — Dimon and inner circle sell ~$170M of stock (Feb 2024)

name: Mary Barra
wealthNote: Neither Forbes nor Bloomberg ranks her. The tier rests on SEC Form 4 data: GM Authority reports she sold 994,863 shares for about $57.9M in the six months to August 2025 and kept 552,238 shares worth about $32.4M. InsiderTrades counts about 5.3M GM shares sold since May 2021 for roughly $273M (pre-tax), plus 428,994 shares (~$33.5M) still held as of July 2026.
humbleBeginnings: Born in 1961 in Royal Oak, Michigan, the daughter of a Finnish-American tool and die maker who worked 39 years at GM's Pontiac division. She started at GM in 1980 at 18 as a co-op student inspecting fender panels and hoods.
breakthrough: She took an electrical engineering degree at the GM Institute (now Kettering University) in 1985 and a Stanford MBA in 1990 on a GM fellowship. She then rose through plant management, manufacturing engineering, HR and global product development. She became CEO on January 14, 2014, the first woman to run a Big Three automaker, and chair on January 6, 2016.
shieldingStrategy: A career employee, not an owner: her wealth is GM stock and stock-based pay, which she has steadily sold down. She took over amid the 2014 ignition-switch crisis, when GM issued 84 recalls covering more than 30 million vehicles.

breakthroughDetail.d: She studied at General Motors Institute (BSEE 1985), then took a Stanford Graduate School of Business MBA (1990) on a GM fellowship.
She was VP of Global Manufacturing Engineering (2008), VP of Global Human Resources (2009–11) and EVP of Global Product Development (2011–13), with purchasing and supply chain added in August 2013.
She became CEO on January 14, 2014 and chair on January 6, 2016.

shieldingDetail.d: On August 28, 2025 she sold 372,024 shares (40.3% of her holdings) for about $21.67M and kept 552,238 shares.
She has been a Disney director since August 2017 and a Stanford trustee.
Like other hired CEOs, she has no control block or super-voting shares. Her stake rises and falls with pay grants and sales.

sources.label: GM Authority — Barra sells 40 percent of her shares
The Walt Disney Company — Mary T. Barra, Director

name: Bob Iger
wealthNote: Not on Forbes or Bloomberg billionaire lists. Wikipedia cites a 2024 estimate of over $700M, built from decades of Disney pay (2023 package $31.6M) and stock awards. Other estimates run $600M–$700M.
humbleBeginnings: Born in New York City in 1951 to an advertising professor and corporate executive and a mother who worked in education. After an Ithaca College TV and radio degree (1973) he joined ABC in 1974 as a production assistant earning $150 a week.
breakthrough: He rose through ABC, which Capital Cities bought in 1985 with Berkshire Hathaway's backing, and became Capital Cities/ABC's president and COO in 1994. He stayed when Disney bought the company in 1996, became Disney's president in 2000 and was CEO from 2005 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2026. As CEO he bought Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm and most of 21st Century Fox.
shieldingStrategy: A hired executive, so his wealth is Disney pay and stock rather than a founder stake. Outside Disney he holds private positions: in 2024 he and his wife Willow Bay took control of Angel City FC, and he sits on startup boards such as Perfect Day and Genies.

breakthroughDetail.d: Disney agreed on January 24, 2006 to buy Pixar for about $7.4B in stock. Steve Jobs, who owned 49.65% of Pixar, became Disney's largest individual shareholder with about 7% and joined its board.
Marvel (about $4B, completed December 2009) and Lucasfilm ($4.05B, December 21, 2012) added the Marvel and Star Wars franchises.

Disney raised its bid for most of 21st Century Fox to $71.3B after Comcast offered $65B in cash, and closed on March 20, 2019. The deal gave Disney control of Hulu. Disney then bought Comcast's 33% Hulu stake for an $8.6B floor price plus $438.7M more in 2025.
He joined Apple's board in November 2011 and resigned on September 10, 2019, as Disney+ and Apple TV+ were about to launch against each other.

shieldingDetail.d: His fortune comes from salary, bonuses and Disney stock awards over two CEO terms, not from a control stake.
In July 2024 he and Willow Bay agreed to buy a controlling stake of at least 35% in Angel City FC at a $250M valuation and committed another $50M. Bay controls the club's board.
Wikipedia lists him on the boards of Perfect Day and Genies.

sources.label: Wikipedia — Acquisition of 21st Century Fox by Disney
TechCrunch — Iger resigns from Apple's board
NBC News — Bay and Iger take controlling stake in Angel City FC

connections.label: outbid for Fox; bought Hulu stake

name: Jack Welch
wealthNote: Wikipedia cites an estimate of $720M in 2006. His retirement package was put at about $417M–$420M.
humbleBeginnings: Born in 1935 in Peabody, Massachusetts, the son of a Boston & Maine Railroad conductor and a homemaker. He studied chemical engineering at UMass Amherst (1957) and took a PhD at the University of Illinois (1960).
breakthrough: He joined GE in 1960 as a junior chemical engineer at $10,500 a year and became chairman and CEO in 1981. Over 20 years he cut management layers, ranked managers and fired the bottom 10% each year, bought RCA (and NBC) for $6.28B in 1986 and grew GE Capital to about 40% of revenue. GE's market value rose from about $14B to as much as $600B, depending on the measure.
shieldingStrategy: His wealth came from GE stock, options and a retirement contract. In 2004 the SEC found GE had not fully disclosed that contract's lifetime perks, including GE aircraft, a Manhattan apartment and cars. GE agreed to a cease-and-desist order without further sanctions.

breakthroughDetail.d: GE bought RCA, owner of NBC, for $6.28B in 1986. NBC became NBCUniversal under GE in 2004, and Comcast bought it in 2011–13.
He expanded GE's finance arm until it produced about 40% of company revenue. In 1988 it became Roger Penske's partner in Penske Truck Leasing.
He cut a nine-layer management hierarchy and fired the bottom 10% of managers each year.
Jeff Immelt beat Bob Nardelli and James McNerney to succeed him in 2000. GE director Ken Langone then recruited Nardelli to run Home Depot.

shieldingDetail.d: His 1996 contract promised lifetime access to company aircraft, cars, offices and apartments. The SEC's September 23, 2004 order found GE's 1997–2002 filings did not fully describe them.
Reported at $417M, with a walk-away package estimated at about $420M by GMI Ratings.
He founded the Jack Welch Management Institute in 2009, and Strayer University acquired it in 2011.

sources.label: SEC — GE settles over former CEO's retirement benefits (2004)
SEC — GE 2011 proxy statement (Penske director since 1994)

name: Alfred P. Sloan Jr.
wealthNote: Fortune's 1957 estimate put his fortune at $200M–$400M, and his lifetime gifts topped $305M by 1966. By U.S. CPI, prices rose about tenfold between the late 1950s–60s and today, so either figure is well over $1B now. The tier uses that inflation-adjusted figure, not a published modern ranking.
humbleBeginnings: Born in New Haven in 1875, the son of a businessman who invested in the Hyatt Roller Bearing Company. He graduated from MIT in electrical engineering in 1895 and joined the struggling Hyatt firm, becoming its president.
breakthrough: He turned Hyatt into a bearing supplier for Oldsmobile and Ford, and in 1916 William Durant's GM bought it for $13.5M, paid largely in stock. Sloan ran the United Motors parts group, which merged into GM in 1918. He became GM's president in 1923, CEO to 1946 and chairman to 1956, and his decentralized divisions with central financial controls took GM's market share from 12% to 52%.
shieldingStrategy: He held GM stock (at one point about 1% of the company) and never sold during the 1920–21 crash. He moved much of his fortune into the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation, which he founded in 1934 and gave $10M in 1937; his gifts topped $305M by 1966.

breakthroughDetail.d: GM bought Hyatt for $13.5M in 1916 as Durant brought suppliers in-house. Archbridge Institute says Sloan and his father split $8M–$9M of it, mostly in stock.
Durant grouped parts makers into United Motors with Sloan as president. It merged into GM in 1918, Durant lost control in 1920 and Sloan became president in 1923.
He set up a price ladder from Chevrolet to Cadillac, annual model changes, consumer financing through GMAC, and decentralized divisions under central financial control.

shieldingDetail.d: At one point he held about 1% of GM and did not sell when the stock fell from $85 to $7 in 1920–21.
The Alfred P. Sloan Foundation (1934) received $10M from him in 1937. It funded MIT's School of Industrial Management in 1952, renamed the Sloan School in 1964, and had $2.2B in assets in 2024.
In 1945 his foundation gave $4M and GM research chief Charles Kettering gave GM stock worth $2M to found the Sloan-Kettering Institute.

sources.label: EBSCO Research Starters — Alfred P. Sloan
Archbridge Institute — The Greatest Businessman in American History
Wikipedia — MIT Sloan School of Management
Wikipedia — Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center

name: Shawn "Jay-Z" Carter
humbleBeginnings: Born December 4, 1969, in Brooklyn and raised in the Marcy Houses public housing project. His father left the family when he was 11, and by his own account he sold crack cocaine as a teenager.
breakthrough: No major label would sign him, so he sold CDs from his car and co-founded Roc-A-Fella Records in 1995 with Damon Dash and Kareem Burke. A 1997 distribution deal with Def Jam led to his presidency of Def Jam (2004–2007), and in 2008 he founded Roc Nation with Live Nation as co-owner.
shieldingStrategy: He takes equity rather than endorsement fees, then sells part of each brand to a strategic buyer while keeping a stake: half of Armand de Brignac to LVMH (2021), a majority of D'Ussé to Bacardi (2023) and control of Tidal to Block (2021) for cash and stock plus a board seat.

breakthroughDetail.d: Roc-A-Fella (1995) put out Reasonable Doubt through Priority Records in 1996, then signed a distribution deal with Def Jam in 1997.
As Def Jam president from 2004 until January 1, 2008, he signed a 16-year-old Rihanna after her audition and helped launch Ne-Yo.
Founded April 1, 2008 as an entertainment company co-owned with Live Nation. It added Roc Nation Sports in 2013.

In January 2015 a company he controlled bought Tidal's parent Aspiro for SEK 466M (about $56M) and relaunched it with 16 artist co-owners. Square (now Block) bought a majority for $297M in cash and stock in March 2021.

shieldingDetail.d: He bought Armand de Brignac champagne in November 2014 and launched D'Ussé cognac with Bacardi in 2012 as a 50/50 venture, rather than taking fees to promote other brands.
LVMH bought 50% of Armand de Brignac in 2021. Bacardi bought a majority of D'Ussé in February 2023 on undisclosed terms, and he kept what it called a 'significant' stake.
The Tidal sale paid partly in Square stock and put him on the company's board, and Forbes lists Block shares among his holdings.
He sold the Rocawear clothing brand, co-founded with Damon Dash in 1999, to Iconix Brand Group for $204M in 2007.

name: Robert L. Johnson
humbleBeginnings: Born April 8, 1946, in Hickory, Mississippi, the ninth of ten children of a schoolteacher and a farmer. He studied at the University of Illinois and Princeton, then worked in Washington for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting and as press secretary to Congressman Walter Fauntroy.
breakthrough: With a $15,000 loan and $500,000 from TCI's John Malone, he and Sheila Johnson launched Black Entertainment Television on January 25, 1980. BET listed on the NYSE in 1991, and Viacom bought it for about $3B in a deal that closed in January 2001, making him the first Black American billionaire.
shieldingStrategy: He took BET private with Liberty Media in 1998, keeping 64%, and was paid by Viacom mostly in stock. He then moved the proceeds into a private holding company, The RLJ Companies, which spans hotels, private equity and car dealerships.

breakthroughDetail.d: Malone's $500,000 tied BET to TCI, the largest cable distributor, so carriage came with the capital. BET started as a programming block on USA Network and became a full channel in September 1982.
BET Holdings went public in 1991, the first Black-controlled television company listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
Viacom agreed to buy BET in 2000 for about $3B, including roughly $2.4B in Viacom stock plus assumed debt, and closed in January 2001. Johnson stayed on as CEO until 2005.

breakthroughDetail.t: First Black majority owner in major US sports.
breakthroughDetail.d: The NBA awarded him the Charlotte expansion franchise (the Bobcats) on December 18, 2002, for a $300M fee. He sold control to Michael Jordan on February 27, 2010.

shieldingDetail.d: In 1998 he and Liberty Media bought out public shareholders, leaving Johnson with 64% and Liberty with 36%. That set up the later sale to Viacom.
Most of the Viacom consideration came as Viacom shares, not cash.
The RLJ Companies holds his interests in banking, private equity, real estate, film, gaming and car dealerships.
RLJ Development, founded in 2000, became RLJ Lodging Trust and went public in 2011. It owns about 100 branded hotels.

name: Oprah Winfrey
humbleBeginnings: Born January 29, 1954, in Kosciusko, Mississippi, to an unmarried teenage mother, she grew up in rural poverty. She later lived in Milwaukee and then in Nashville with her father, a barber.
breakthrough: In 1984 she took over WLS-TV's struggling AM Chicago, which went into national syndication through King World in 1986 as The Oprah Winfrey Show. She founded Harpo Productions that year, and in 1988 took ownership of the show itself, so she was its owner as well as its host until it ended in 2011.
shieldingStrategy: She owns the content through Harpo instead of working as hired talent. She launched OWN as a 50/50 joint venture with Discovery, then sold most of her stake to Discovery for company shares. Forbes also counts California and Hawaii real estate, including about 2,100 acres in Hawaii.

breakthroughDetail.d: Harpo, founded in 1986, took over production of the talk show from ABC's WLS-TV in 1988 and opened Harpo Studios in Chicago in 1990.
Harpo co-produced films including Beloved (1998), Selma (2014) and the 2023 The Color Purple.
Announced with Discovery in 2008, OWN replaced Discovery Health on January 1, 2011. It lost an estimated $330M by May 2012 before scripted shows from Tyler Perry turned it around.
She joined WeightWatchers' board in 2015 with a 10% stake and left it on February 28, 2024.

shieldingDetail.d: Owning the show's rights through Harpo, rather than drawing a host's salary, is how Forbes traces most of her fortune.
Discovery raised its OWN stake to about 74% in 2017 and to 95% in December 2020, leaving Harpo with 5%. Forbes says she took company shares in exchange.
Her holdings in California and Hawaii include about 2,100 acres in Hawaii (Forbes).
In 2024 she said she would donate all her remaining WeightWatchers stock to the National Museum of African American History and Culture.

sources.label: Global News — Oprah Winfrey leaves WeightWatchers board

name: Tyler Perry
humbleBeginnings: Born Emmitt Perry Jr. in New Orleans in 1969, he grew up with an abusive father and changed his first name at 16. He put his $12,000 of savings into his first musical, I Know I've Been Changed, in Atlanta in 1992.
breakthrough: After years of reworking, the show succeeded in Atlanta in 1998, and his touring plays built the audience for Diary of a Mad Black Woman (2005), which grossed $50.6M domestically. In 2006 TBS ordered 100 episodes of House of Payne for about $200M, and his films, led by the Madea series, have grossed more than $660M.
shieldingStrategy: Forbes says he owns 100% of the content he has created. He licenses shows to networks and streamers (TBS, OWN, BET, Netflix, Amazon) through overall deals instead of selling the rights, and he owns Tyler Perry Studios outright.

breakthroughDetail.d: The TBS order for 100 episodes (2006) was followed by an exclusive scripted deal with OWN in October 2012, which produced The Haves and the Have Nots, and then a multiyear Viacom/BET deal in 2017.

He bought 330 acres of the former Fort McPherson army base in Atlanta in 2015 and opened Tyler Perry Studios there in 2019, with 12 soundstages. He was the first African American to own a major film studio outright.
He co-owned BET+, which launched in 2019 as a joint venture between BET and Tyler Perry Studios, with a stake of about 25%.
Forbes notes a 2022 four-picture deal with Amazon and ongoing production for Netflix.

shieldingDetail.d: Networks pay for production and distribution while he keeps ownership of the content.
The studio sits on land he owns, not leased stages. He bought his earlier sites in 2006 (99 Krog Street, $7M) and in 2008, and sold the southwest Atlanta site in 2018.
On March 13, 2026, Paramount Skydance bought his BET+ stake for an undisclosed sum (Deadline: tens of millions) and folded the service into Paramount+. His overall deal continues.

sources.label: TheWrap — Paramount buys out Tyler Perry's stake in BET+

name: Robyn "Rihanna" Fenty
humbleBeginnings: Born February 20, 1988, in Saint Michael, Barbados, she grew up with a father who struggled with addiction. Producer Evan Rogers discovered her in 2003, when she was singing with two classmates.
breakthrough: At 16 she auditioned for Jay-Z, then president of Def Jam, and signed with the label. She used her music fame to launch Fenty Beauty with LVMH's Kendo incubator in September 2017. It sold $72M in its first month.
shieldingStrategy: She owns about half of Fenty Beauty in a 50/50 venture with LVMH, which supplies manufacturing and distribution through Kendo and Sephora. She also co-founded Savage X Fenty with TechStyle and let outside rounds dilute her stake while raising its valuation.

breakthroughDetail.d: Fenty Beauty's Pro Filt'r foundation targeted women of color whom other brands had ignored. Sales reached about €500M by the end of 2018.
Wikipedia cites a valuation of about $2.8B for the whole business, half of it hers. Forbes attributes her billionaire status mainly to the brand.
She launched the lingerie brand with TechStyle Fashion Group in May 2018. It reached a $1B valuation in 2021 and raised $125M more in January 2022.

shieldingDetail.d: LVMH holds the other half of Fenty Beauty and makes the products through Kendo, so she does not carry the manufacturing capital.
Forbes estimates her Savage X Fenty stake at about 28% after outside rounds, including the $125M raised in 2022.
She stepped down as Savage X Fenty CEO in June 2023 and kept her stake.

name: Earvin "Magic" Johnson
humbleBeginnings: Born August 14, 1959, in Lansing, Michigan, to Earvin Sr., a General Motors assembly worker, and Christine, a school janitor. Before the 1979 draft he turned down Nike stock and royalties for $100,000 a year in cash from Converse.
breakthrough: While still playing for the Lakers he bought the D.C. Pepsi bottler with Earl Graves (1990), his first deal beyond endorsements. After retiring he ran Magic Johnson Enterprises as a joint-venture machine in urban markets: theaters with Loews, Starbucks, and the Canyon-Johnson real estate funds. A controlling stake in EquiTrust Life Insurance (2015) made him a billionaire, only the fourth athlete Forbes has counted.
shieldingStrategy: He lends his brand and urban-market access to partners that supply the operating system and capital, such as Pepsi, Loews, Starbucks, Canyon Capital, Guggenheim and Ron Burkle. He then sells his side back when a venture matures. Most of his wealth now sits in his 60% of EquiTrust (Forbes).

breakthroughDetail.d: On July 25, 1990, he and Graves bought control of Pepsi-Cola of Washington, D.C., L.P. for $60M, then the largest minority-owned Pepsi bottler. He had endorsed Pepsi since 1989.

In 1998 his Johnson Development Corp. and Starbucks formed Urban Coffee Opportunities, a 50/50 venture that opened more than 100 stores, including Harlem. Starbucks bought out his half in October 2010.
Magic Johnson Enterprises was a founding member of Guggenheim Baseball Management, which bought the Los Angeles Dodgers from Frank McCourt for $2.15B in 2012.
YMF Media, controlled by Ron Burkle with Johnson on its board, bought 15 Inner City Broadcasting stations, including WBLS, for a $180M credit bid in 2012.

shieldingDetail.d: EquiTrust, in which he bought a controlling interest in June 2015, grew from $16B to $33B in assets. Forbes credits most of his fortune to his 60% stake.
He sold his Urban Coffee stores back to Starbucks (2010) and Graves sold the bottler to Pepsi (1998), so in both cases the brand owner bought out the local partner.
He holds small stakes in the Dodgers, the Washington Commanders, the Los Angeles Sparks and LAFC rather than control positions (Forbes).

sources.label: UPI — Magic Johnson buys into D.C.-area Pepsi bottling operation (1990)
Nation's Restaurant News — Starbucks, Magic Johnson end urban coffee partnership
RBR — Inner City buy puts Magic in six markets

name: Soul Train

name: H.J. Russell & Company
description: Herman Russell's Atlanta firm (founded 1953), the largest minority-owned real-estate and construction company in the U.S.

name: Concessions International
description: Russell's airport food and beverage operator; majority control moved to trusts for his children in 2013.

name: Citizens Trust Bank
description: Atlanta Black-owned bank. H.J. Russell built its 1969 headquarters, and Russell sat on its board.

name: The Coca-Cola Company
description: Atlanta-based beverage maker; H.J. Russell & Company worked on its headquarters, completed in 1987.

name: Ariel Investments

name: The ActOne Group

name: Inner City Broadcasting Corp.

name: Paul Quinn College

name: Barden Companies
description: Don Barden's private holding company for cable, casino, real-estate and international ventures; $347M in revenue in 2003.

name: Majestic Star Casino
description: Barden's casino LLC (Gary, Tunica, Black Hawk, Las Vegas Fitzgeralds); filed for bankruptcy in 2009.

name: Comcast

name: Madam C.J. Walker Manufacturing Co.

name: Poro College

name: Independent Order of St. Luke

name: Overton Hygienic Manufacturing Co.

name: Victory Life Insurance Co.

name: Binga State Bank

name: Chicago Defender

name: Pittsburgh Courier
