description: Andrew Carnegie's steel partnership, formed July 1, 1892, with Frick, Lauder and Phipps. Morgan bought it in 1901 and it ran as a U.S. Steel subsidiary under the same name for 35 years.

name: General Electric
description: Formed April 15, 1892, when J.P. Morgan merged Edison General Electric and Thomson-Houston. After the 2023–24 breakup its legal successor is GE Aerospace, whose official GICS sub-industry is used here.

name: New York Central Railroad
description: Vanderbilt took control in 1867 and merged it with the Hudson River Railroad in 1869. In 1879 Morgan sold a large block of William H. Vanderbilt's shares and joined its board. It merged into Penn Central in 1968.

name: Pennsylvania Railroad
description: Where Andrew Carnegie rose from telegrapher to division superintendent under Thomas A. Scott. In 1885 Morgan brokered its truce with the New York Central over the West Shore and South Pennsylvania lines.

name: Northern Securities Company
description: Holding company formed in 1901 by J.P. Morgan, James J. Hill and E.H. Harriman for the Great Northern, Northern Pacific and Burlington railroads. The Supreme Court ordered it dissolved under the Sherman Act on March 14, 1904.

name: Vanderbilt University
description: Founded in Nashville in 1873 with Cornelius Vanderbilt's $1M gift, then the largest charitable gift in U.S. history.

name: Carnegie Corporation of New York
description: Founded by Andrew Carnegie in 1911 with $135M. It was renamed the Andrew Carnegie Foundation on June 9, 2026, and its endowment is about $5B.

name: Carnegie Mellon University
description: Founded by Andrew Carnegie in 1900 as the Carnegie Technical Schools in Pittsburgh. It merged with the Mellon Institute in 1967.

name: Google (Alphabet)
description: Founded by Page and Brin in 1998 and part of Alphabet since 2015. Class B shares carry 10 votes, which keeps the founders in control. It invested in SpaceX in 2015 and held about 6% after the 2026 IPO.

name: Tesla
description: Founded in 2003 by Eberhard and Tarpenning. Musk led its 2004 Series A, and Page and Brin invested in 2006. Goldman Sachs co-led its 2010 IPO, and it moved its incorporation to Texas in 2024.

name: SpaceX
description: Founded by Musk in 2002. Google and Fidelity invested $1B in 2015. It bought xAI in February 2026 and listed on Nasdaq (SPCX) on June 12, 2026, with Musk keeping super-voting control.

name: xAI
description: Musk's AI company, announced in July 2023. It absorbed X Corp in March 2025 and became a SpaceX subsidiary in February 2026. Grok 2 was trained on Oracle cloud GPUs.

name: X (Twitter)
description: Twitter, which Musk took private on Oct 27, 2022 for about $44B. It was merged into xAI in March 2025.

name: PayPal
description: Formed in 2000 when Musk's X.com merged with Confinity. eBay bought it for $1.5B in 2002. It is now an S&P 500 company.

name: eBay
description: Bought PayPal for $1.5B in 2002, which gave Musk about $175.8M.

name: Zip2
description: Web software firm co-founded in 1995 by Elon and Kimbal Musk and Greg Kouri. Compaq bought it for $307M in cash in 1999.

name: OpenAI
description: Founded in December 2015 as a nonprofit. Musk co-founded it partly as a counterweight to Google's AI work, and Isaacson reports it ended his friendship with Larry Page.

name: Fidelity Investments
description: Privately held fund firm that co-led SpaceX's $1B round with Google in January 2015.

name: Kleiner Perkins
description: Co-led Google's $25M round in June 1999. Partner John Doerr sits on Alphabet's board.

name: Sequoia Capital
description: Co-led Google's $25M round in June 1999. Partner Michael Moritz joined the Giving Pledge in 2012, in the same group as Musk and John Sall.

name: Bayshore Global Management
description: Sergey Brin's family office, founded in 2005 and based in Palo Alto with a Singapore office. It manages about $100B and the Sergey Brin Family Foundation.

name: Koop
description: Larry Page's private family office. It has no website and was reincorporated in Delaware in December 2025.

name: Musk Foundation
description: Musk's foundation, which received a large gift of Tesla shares in 2021 and held over $14B in assets at the end of 2024.

name: Anthropic
description: Founded in 2021 by seven former OpenAI staff led by Dario and Daniela Amodei. It is a Delaware public benefit corporation overseen partly by a Long-Term Benefit Trust. It was valued at $965B in May 2026 and filed confidential IPO papers in June 2026. Tagged Application Software as the closest fit, because it sells Claude subscriptions and API access, matching how openai and xai are tagged.

name: Palantir Technologies
description: Founded May 6, 2003 by Thiel, Karp, Stephen Cohen, Joe Lonsdale and Nathan Gettings, with early money from Thiel and the CIA's In-Q-Tel. It direct-listed in 2020, joined the S&P 500 in 2024, and its Class F shares give the founders 49.999999% of the vote.

name: Founders Fund
description: San Francisco VC firm started in 2005 by Thiel, Ken Howery and Luke Nosek, with about $17B under management in 2025. It was the first institutional investor in SpaceX and Palantir and an early Facebook investor.

name: Y Combinator
description: Founded in March 2005 by Paul Graham, Jessica Livingston, Robert Morris and Trevor Blackwell, and has funded more than 5,000 startups. Its alumni include Loopt (first batch), Airbnb, Stripe and Reddit.

name: Loopt
description: Mobile geosocial app co-founded in 2005 by Sam Altman, Nick Sivo and Alok Deshpande. Sequoia and NEA led its Series A, and Green Dot bought it for $43.4M in March 2012.

name: Hydrazine Capital
description: Venture firm Sam and Jack Altman co-founded in 2012. Its first fund raised $21M with Peter Thiel as the main backer and invested mostly in YC companies.

name: Stripe
description: Private payments company and Y Combinator alumnus. Daniela Amodei joined in 2013 as an early employee, Sam Altman is an early investor, and Founders Fund holds a stake. It was valued at $159B in February 2026 (Forbes). Tagged by its closest listed peers.

name: Amazon
description: Jeff Bezos's company, #2 on the 2025 Fortune 500. It invested $8B in Anthropic in 2023–24, and AWS was one of the backers that pledged $1B to OpenAI at its 2015 founding.

name: Microsoft
description: Co-founded by Bill Gates in 1975 and #14 on the 2025 Fortune 500. It invested in OpenAI from 2019 and held about 27% after OpenAI's 2025 restructuring. In November 2025 it committed up to $5B to Anthropic.

name: Nvidia
description: Co-founded by Jensen Huang in 1993 and #31 on the 2025 Fortune 500. In September 2025 it signed a letter of intent to supply OpenAI with 10GW of systems and invest up to $100B, and in November 2025 it committed up to $10B to Anthropic.

name: Meta Platforms (Facebook)
description: Facebook, founded by Mark Zuckerberg in 2004 and #22 on the 2025 Fortune 500. Peter Thiel made its first outside investment ($500K for 10.2%) in 2004 and sat on its board until 2022.

name: Berkshire Hathaway
description: Former New Bedford textile maker that Buffett took control of in 1965 and turned into an insurance-funded conglomerate (Geico, Duracell, Dairy Queen) with large stakes in Apple, American Express, Coca-Cola and Bank of America. Greg Abel became CEO in 2026.

name: Blackstone
description: Founded in 1985 by Peter Peterson and Stephen Schwarzman with $400,000. Now the world's largest alternative-asset manager (about $1.3T), spanning buyouts, real estate and credit. Public since 2007.

name: KKR
description: Kohlberg Kravis Roberts, founded in 1976 by ex-Bear Stearns bankers Jerome Kohlberg, Henry Kravis and George Roberts. It made the leveraged buyout famous with Beatrice and RJR Nabisco. Listed on the NYSE in 2010 and joined the S&P 500 in 2024.

name: Apollo Global Management
description: Founded in 1990 by Drexel Burnham Lambert alumni Leon Black, Josh Harris and Marc Rowan. Built on distressed-to-control investing and Athene's retirement annuities, it passed $1T in assets in 2026.

name: Charles Schwab Corporation
description: Discount brokerage founded in San Francisco in 1971 (as First Commander, renamed 1973). Owned by Bank of America from 1983 to 1987, public since 1987, and bought TD Ameritrade in 2020.

name: Interactive Brokers
description: Electronic broker that grew out of Thomas Peterffy's market maker Timber Hill. Public since 2007 but controlled by Peterffy, and added to the S&P 500 in August 2025.

name: Icahn Enterprises
description: Nasdaq-listed master limited partnership (formerly American Real Estate Partners), about 86% owned by Carl Icahn, holding energy (CVR), automotive, food packaging and real-estate businesses.

name: RJR Nabisco
description: Its 1988–89 buyout by KKR for about $25B (about $31B including debt), partly financed with Drexel junk bonds, was the largest LBO in history until the mid-2000s. Carl Icahn later fought to split it. Its tobacco and food businesses were separated in 1999.

name: Beatrice Foods
description: Chicago food conglomerate bought by KKR in 1986 and broken up. Its international arm was sold to Reginald Lewis's TLC Group in 1987 for $985M, and the rest went to ConAgra in 1990.

name: Caesars Entertainment
description: Casino company (formerly Harrah's). Apollo and TPG took it private in 2008 for about $27.8B, and Carl Icahn's 2019 stake and board seats pushed it into the Eldorado merger.

name: Trans World Airlines (TWA)
description: U.S. airline that Carl Icahn took control of in 1985 and bought outright in a 1988 LBO, selling off assets such as its London routes.

name: Hilton Worldwide
description: Hotel company that Blackstone bought for about $26B (including debt) in 2007, took public again in 2013 and fully exited in 2018 with about $14B of profit.

name: Bank of America
description: Owned Charles Schwab's brokerage from 1983 to 1987. Berkshire Hathaway's 2011 $5B preferred investment became one of its largest stakes.

name: Apple
description: iPhone and Mac maker and one of Berkshire Hathaway's largest stock holdings. Carl Icahn held a stake from 2013 to 2016 and campaigned for buybacks.

name: Lehman Brothers
description: Wall Street bank where Stephen Schwarzman ran M&A and Peter Peterson had worked before they founded Blackstone in 1985. It collapsed in 2008.

name: Bear Stearns
description: Investment bank where Jerome Kohlberg, Henry Kravis and George Roberts did early bootstrap buyouts before leaving to form KKR in 1976. Sold to JPMorgan Chase in 2008.

name: Gates Foundation
description: Bill Gates's foundation, plans to close by 2045. Warren Buffett gave it about $48B in Berkshire stock from 2006 and was a trustee until 2021, but stopped giving to it in 2026.

name: Columbia University
description: New York university. Buffett earned his economics master's at Columbia Business School under Benjamin Graham, and Henry Kravis (MBA 1969) gave the business school $100M.

name: Claremont McKenna College
description: Liberal-arts college in California and alma mater of both KKR cousins. George Roberts gave it $190M across 2012 and 2022.

name: University of Pennsylvania
description: Home of the Wharton School, where Marc Rowan earned his BS and MBA and gave $50M (2018), and where Warren Buffett studied from 1947 to 1949.

name: Nike
description: Founded as Blue Ribbon Sports on Jan 25, 1964 by Phil Knight and Bill Bowerman; renamed Nike in 1971 and listed in 1980. Class A shares, held through Swoosh, LLC, elect three-quarters of the board. Ariel's John Rogers Jr. was a director from 2018 to 2026.

name: Ralph Lauren Corporation
description: Started in 1967 with men's ties; listed on the NYSE on June 12, 1997. A Goldman Sachs fund bought 28% for $135M in 1994. Ranked #537 on Fortune's 2025 list, so it is outside the Fortune 500.

name: Airbnb
description: Founded in 2008 by Chesky, Gebbia and Blecharczyk. Backed by Y Combinator (2009), Sequoia, Greylock and Founders Fund; IPO Dec 10, 2020 raised $3.5B. Sequoia's Alfred Lin joined its board in 2012.

name: DoorDash
description: Founded in 2013 by Stanford students. Sequoia led its $17.3M Series A in 2014 and Alfred Lin joined the board, so it shares a Sequoia board member with Airbnb. It bought Caviar from Square (2019), Wolt (2021) and Deliveroo (2025).

name: Carvana
description: Started in 2012 inside DriveTime and listed in April 2017. It sells its auto loans to Ally under a forward-flow agreement, restructured its bonds with Apollo-led holders in 2023 and joined the S&P 500 on Dec 22, 2025.

name: DriveTime
description: Ernest Garcia II bought the bankrupt Ugly Duckling rent-a-car franchise in 1991, listed it in 1996 and took it private in 2002 as DriveTime. Its affiliate Bridgecrest services loans. It funded Carvana's start.

name: Ally Financial
description: Former GMAC. Since December 2016 it has bought Carvana's auto loans under a master purchase agreement, recently committing up to $4B a year.

name: Wayfair
description: Founded in 2002 as CSN Stores by Niraj Shah and Steve Conine, Cornell roommates. Bootstrapped until 2011 and listed on the NYSE in October 2014. Class B shares carry ten votes.

name: Penske Corporation
description: Roger Penske's private holding company (1969), with interests in auto retail, truck leasing, logistics and motorsport, and 67% of Penske Entertainment (Fox holds 33%).

name: Penske Automotive Group
description: Began as United Auto Group (1990) and renamed in 2007. It sells brands including Toyota, Lexus, Honda and Mercedes-Benz and owns 28.9% of Penske Truck Leasing.

name: Penske Truck Leasing
description: Founded Dec 1, 1969. A GE Capital partnership from 1988, when GE contributed Gelco Truck Leasing; GE sold out in 2015–17. Owned 41.1% by Penske Corp., 28.9% by PAG and 30% by Mitsui.

name: Mitsui & Co.
description: Bought 20% of Penske Truck Leasing from GE Capital in 2015 for about $750M, then most of GE's last 15.5% in 2017.

name: Detroit Diesel
description: GM's diesel engine unit. Penske took 60% in 1988 and rebuilt its market share; it was sold to DaimlerChrysler in 2000.

name: General Motors
description: Detroit automaker. Roger Penske built his business on a Chevrolet dealership and took control of GM's Detroit Diesel unit in 1988.

name: Indianapolis Motor Speedway
description: Home of the Indianapolis 500. The Hulman family sold it and IndyCar to Penske on Nov 4, 2019; it is now held through Penske Entertainment.

name: D.R. Horton
description: Founded in 1978 in Fort Worth, listed in 1992 and the largest U.S. homebuilder by volume since 2002. Based in Arlington, Texas.

name: Forestar Group
description: D.R. Horton bought 75% of it for $558.3M in October 2017. A master supply agreement gives Horton first offer on its lots; Forestar is a NYSE 'controlled company'.

name: University of Oregon
description: Phil Knight's alma mater (1959), where Bill Bowerman coached him; Knight has given it over $2B.

name: Blue Origin
description: Bezos's privately held space company, founded in 2000 and funded by roughly $1B a year of his Amazon share sales. Forbes values it at about $130B.

name: The Washington Post
description: Bought by Jeff Bezos for $250M in 2013 through his holding company Nash Holdings.

name: LinkedIn
description: Founded in December 2002 by Reid Hoffman and former PayPal colleagues. Sequoia led its 2003 Series A, and Sequoia and Greylock joined a 2008 round at about $1B. Microsoft bought it for $26.2B, closing Dec 8, 2016.

name: Dell Technologies
description: Founded in 1984 as PC's Limited. It was taken private in 2013 with Silver Lake and a $2B Microsoft loan, bought EMC for $67B in 2016 and relisted in 2018. It builds Nvidia-based AI servers, including servers for xAI's Memphis supercomputer.

name: Silver Lake
description: Technology buyout firm that took Dell private with Michael Dell in 2013 for $24.4B. In June 2026 it still held 7.2% of Dell's stock and 13% of the votes.

name: Salesforce
description: Founded in March 1999 by ex-Oracle executive Marc Benioff and others, with seed money from Larry Ellison. It listed in 2004 and bought Tableau ($15.7B) and Slack ($27.7B).

name: Netflix
description: Founded in 1997 by Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph, listed in 2002 and streaming since 2007. It paid Comcast for direct interconnection in 2014. In Feb 2026 it lost Warner Bros. Discovery to Paramount Skydance and received a $2.8B termination fee.

name: Block (Square)
description: Founded as Square in 2009 by Jack Dorsey and Jim McKelvey. It listed in 2015, was renamed Block in 2021, bought Afterpay for $29B and joined the S&P 500 in July 2025.

name: Paramount Skydance
description: Formed in August 2025 when David Ellison's Skydance merged with Paramount Global, financed by the Ellison family trust; Larry Ellison owns nearly 50%. In 2026 it outbid Netflix for Warner Bros. Discovery at $31 a share (over $110B including debt).

name: Cascade Investment
description: Bill Gates's private investment firm, founded in 1995 and run by Michael Larson. It holds 71% of Four Seasons, large stakes in Republic Services, Ecolab, Canadian National and Deere, and about 269,000 acres of U.S. farmland.

name: Chan Zuckerberg Initiative
description: Founded Dec 1, 2015 by Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan as an LLC rather than a foundation, to receive 99% of their Facebook shares over their lifetimes. It funds the Biohub and science, education and housing work.

name: Energy Transfer
description: Founded in 1996 by Kelcy Warren and Ray Davis with about 200 miles of East Texas pipe. Through Sunoco, Southern Union, Regency and Crestwood it grew to about 130,000-140,000 miles. It owns 36.4% of Dakota Access.

name: Kinder Morgan
description: Formed in 1997 when Richard Kinder and William Morgan bought Enron Liquids Pipeline's general partner for $40M. It was taken private in 2007 and re-listed in 2011 (then the largest PE-backed US IPO), and grew to about 78,000 miles of pipeline.

name: Enron
description: Formed in 1985 by merging Houston Natural Gas and InterNorth into the second-largest US gas pipeline system. Richard Kinder was president from 1990 to 1996. It filed for bankruptcy on December 2, 2001, after accounting fraud.

name: Continental Resources
description: Founded in 1967 as Shelly Dean Oil and renamed in 1990. It opened up the North Dakota Bakken with horizontal fracked wells, listed in 2007, and was taken private by the Hamm family for $4.3B in 2022. (Fortune ranked it 503rd in 2025, just outside the 500.)

name: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals
description: Founded in 1988 by Leonard Schleifer and George Yancopoulos, IPO 1991. It makes Eylea, Dupixent and Libtayo, partnered with Sanofi from 2007, and has a dual-class structure with ten-vote Class A stock.

name: Universal Health Services
description: Founded by Alan B. Miller in King of Prussia in 1979 and listed in 1981. It runs acute-care hospitals and more than 300 behavioral-health facilities in the US and UK, and the Miller family controls it through super-voting Class C stock.

name: Tele-Communications Inc. (TCI)
description: Founded by Bob Magness in Denver in 1968, run by John Malone from 1973, and the largest US cable company by 1982. AT&T bought it in 1999 for $32B in stock plus $16B of debt, and it became AT&T Broadband.

name: Liberty Media
description: Spun out of TCI in 1991 and controlled by John Malone through Class B shares. It specializes in tax-free spinoffs and tracking stocks, owns Formula One (2017) and MotoGP (2025), and earlier co-owned QVC with Comcast and held 47.9% of DirecTV.

name: AT&T
description: Bought TCI in 1999 and turned its systems into AT&T Broadband, which it sold to Comcast in 2002. In 2025 it agreed to buy EchoStar spectrum for $23B.

name: EchoStar
description: Co-founded in 1980 by Charlie Ergen, Candy Ergen and Jim DeFranco. It created DISH Network (spun off in 2008, recombined in 2023) and sold spectrum to AT&T ($23B) and SpaceX (about $17B, half in stock) in 2025.

name: Career Communications Group
description: Baltimore-based private publisher founded by Tyrone Taborn in the mid-1980s. It publishes US Black Engineer & IT, Hispanic Engineer & IT and Women of Color, and runs the BEYA and Women of Color STEM conferences.

name: BEYA STEM Conference
description: The Black Engineer of the Year Awards, co-founded by Tyrone Taborn and Morgan State dean Eugene DeLoatch and first held at Morgan State in February 1987. It is co-hosted by CCG, the HBCU engineering deans and Lockheed Martin, and draws more than 10,000 attendees and 100+ recruiting companies.

name: Lockheed Martin
description: Long-time co-host of the BEYA STEM Conference, alongside CCG and the Council of Engineering Deans of the HBCUs.

name: Johns Hopkins University
description: Baltimore research university. John Malone earned an MS and a PhD in operations research there, and Tyrone Taborn holds a BS from it.

name: Turner Broadcasting System
description: Ted Turner's Atlanta company, built from his father's billboard business, which owned WTBS, CNN, TNT, Cartoon Network and the MGM library. Cable operators led by TCI took 37% in 1987. It merged into Time Warner in 1996 and is now part of Warner Bros. Discovery.

name: CNN
description: Cable News Network, launched by Ted Turner in June 1980 as the first 24-hour live news channel. It passed to Time Warner in 1996 and now belongs to Warner Bros. Discovery.

name: Atlanta Braves
description: Major League Baseball team owned by Ted Turner and TBS from 1976, by Time Warner from 1996 and by Liberty Media from May 2007. In 2023 Liberty split it off as Atlanta Braves Holdings.

name: Time Warner
description: Formed in 1990 when Time Inc. merged with Warner Communications. It bought Turner Broadcasting in 1996 and merged with AOL in 2001, and in 2002 AOL Time Warner reported a $99B loss. AT&T bought it for $85.4B in 2018 and renamed it WarnerMedia, which merged with Discovery in 2022.

name: Warner Bros. Discovery
description: Formed in April 2022 when AT&T's WarnerMedia merged with Discovery. It owns the former Turner networks, including CNN, TNT and Cartoon Network.

name: United Nations Foundation
description: Washington, D.C. charity set up in 1998 to channel Ted Turner's $1B pledge of September 1997, paid at about $100M a year for 10 years, in support of UN causes.

name: Las Vegas Sands
description: Founded by Sheldon Adelson around the 1988–89 Sands Hotel purchase. It built The Venetian (1999), Sands Macao (2004) and Marina Bay Sands (2010), and went public in December 2004. It sold its Las Vegas Strip assets in 2022 to focus on Macau and Singapore, and the Adelson family holds about 54%.

name: COMDEX
description: The COMputer Dealers' EXhibition, launched in Las Vegas in 1979 by Adelson's Interface Group. Attendance peaked at 225,000 in 1996. It was sold to SoftBank in 1995 for about $860M and ended in 2003.

name: Galaxy Entertainment Group
description: Hong Kong-listed operator that won a 2002 Macau gaming concession with Las Vegas Sands. When the partnership split, Macau let Sands run under its own sub-concession, which became the model for the market's six operators.

name: HCA Healthcare
description: Hospital Corporation of America, founded in Nashville in 1968 by Thomas Frist Sr., Thomas Frist Jr. and Jack Massey. It went private in 1988, merged into Columbia/HCA in 1994, and was taken private in the record $33B 2006 buyout by KKR, Bain, Merrill Lynch and the Frists before its 2011 re-IPO. It runs about 190 hospitals.

name: Bain Capital
description: Boston private equity firm spun out of Bain & Company in 1984. It was a lead sponsor, with KKR and Merrill Lynch, of the $33B 2006 HCA buyout.

name: FedEx
description: Founded by Fred Smith as Federal Express in 1971 and flying from Memphis in 1973 on about $72M of institutional venture money. It grew through Flying Tigers, Caliber/RPS, Kinko's and TNT Express, and spun off FedEx Freight in June 2026.

name: General Dynamics
description: Defense contractor based in Reston, Virginia. It invested in Federal Express's record 1973 venture round, but its board later turned down Fred Smith's request for further funding.

name: Walmart
description: Founded by Sam Walton in Rogers, Arkansas, in 1962; IPO 1970, NYSE 1972, moved to Nasdaq in December 2025. #1 on the 2025 Fortune 500, a spot it has held every year since 2002 except 2006, 2009 and 2012. The Walton family controls about 45%.

name: Walton Enterprises
description: Formed in 1953 as a Walton family partnership, now an LLC and the family office. It holds 37.3% of Walmart and has owned banks including Arvest.

name: Walton Family Foundation
description: Set up by Sam and Helen Walton in 1987, on Walmart's 25th anniversary; best known for funding charter schools and, later, water and environmental work.

name: Stephens Inc.
description: Little Rock investment bank that, with White Weld & Co., took Wal-Mart public on October 1, 1970 at $16.50 a share.

name: JCPenney
description: Where Sam Walton trained as a management trainee in 1940 at $75 a month.

name: Denver Broncos
description: Bought by a Rob Walton-led group for $4.65B in 2022, then a record for a sports team; Greg Penner is CEO and controlling owner, and partners include Condoleezza Rice, Mellody Hobson and Lewis Hamilton.

name: Best Buy
description: Started by Richard Schulze as Sound of Music in Saint Paul in 1966 and renamed Best Buy around 1983. #108 on the 2025 Fortune 500.

name: Richard M. Schulze Family Foundation
description: Formed in 2002; by 2018 one of Minnesota's five largest private foundations.

name: The Home Depot
description: Founded in 1978 by Bernie Marcus, Arthur Blank, Ken Langone, Pat Farrah and Ron Brill; first stores opened in Atlanta June 22, 1979. Listed on Nasdaq in 1981 and the NYSE in 1984. Hired GE's Bob Nardelli as CEO in 2000. #24 on the 2025 Fortune 500.

name: Handy Dan Home Improvement Centers
description: Daylin-owned West Coast chain run by Bernie Marcus, with Arthur Blank as finance VP; both were fired in 1978 and founded The Home Depot.

name: Invemed Associates
description: Ken Langone's private New York investment bank, founded in 1974, which raised the starting capital for The Home Depot.

name: Electronic Data Systems (EDS)
description: Ross Perot's computer services firm, taken public in 1968 by R.W. Pressprich after Ken Langone won Perot's mandate.

name: New York Stock Exchange
description: Ken Langone sat on its board and its compensation committee (1999-2003), which approved Richard Grasso's pay package. Now owned by Intercontinental Exchange.

name: NYU Langone Health
description: NYU's medical center, renamed after Ken Langone's $200M gift; he later pledged $100M toward free tuition at its medical school (2018).

name: Atlanta Falcons
description: Bought by Arthur Blank in February 2002 for $545M; shares Mercedes-Benz Stadium with Atlanta United.

name: Atlanta United FC
description: MLS expansion club founded by Arthur Blank that began play in 2017.

name: Arthur M. Blank Family Foundation
description: Arthur Blank's main philanthropic vehicle; its gifts include $200M to Children's Healthcare of Atlanta.

name: Georgia Aquarium
description: Atlanta aquarium built with a $250M gift from Bernie Marcus.

name: Starbucks
description: Founded in Seattle in 1971 by Jerry Baldwin, Zev Siegl and Gordon Bowker and bought in 1987 by Howard Schultz's Il Giornale for $3.8M. IPO June 1992. Ran Urban Coffee Opportunities, a 50/50 venture with Magic Johnson, from 1998 to 2010. #126 on the 2025 Fortune 500.

name: Il Giornale
description: Howard Schultz's Milan-style espresso bars, opened in Seattle in April 1986 with $150,000 from Starbucks among its backers; it bought Starbucks in 1987 and took its name.

name: Seattle SuperSonics
description: Owned by Howard Schultz's group from 2001 until 2006, when it was sold with the WNBA's Storm for $350M to Clay Bennett's Oklahoma City group.

name: Maveron
description: Consumer-focused venture firm co-founded in 1998 by Howard Schultz and Dan Levitan; early backer of eBay.

name: The Estée Lauder Companies
description: Founded in 1946 by Estée and Joseph Lauder and listed on the NYSE in November 1995 with dual-class shares; the family holds about 38% of the equity and 86% of the votes. Brands include Clinique, M.A.C, La Mer, Aveda and Tom Ford (bought 2022 for $2.8B). #279 on the 2025 Fortune 500.

name: Saks Fifth Avenue
description: Manhattan department store that gave Estée Lauder her first major account in 1948.

name: AMD
description: Advanced Micro Devices, founded in 1969 by Jerry Sanders and other Fairchild alumni. It went fabless in 2008–09 with the GlobalFoundries spin-off. Under Lisa Su (CEO from 2014) it grew from about $3B in market value to over $1T, buying Xilinx (2022) and ZT Systems. In October 2025 it agreed to supply OpenAI with 6GW of GPUs and gave OpenAI a warrant for up to 160M shares. It ranked #167 on the 2025 Fortune 500 (per AMD's own announcement).

name: TSMC
description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, founded in 1987 by Morris Chang in Hsinchu and the world's largest dedicated foundry. It makes chips for Apple, its largest customer at about 26% of 2021 revenue, as well as Nvidia and others. Apple is the anchor customer of its Arizona fabs. It is not an S&P 500 member, so its GICS tag is inferred.

name: Beats Electronics
description: Co-founded by Dr. Dre and Jimmy Iovine. In 2014 Apple bought it for $3B ($2.6B upfront plus about $400M vesting over time), Apple's largest acquisition, and hired both founders. Beats Music was folded into Apple Music in 2015, and Beats remains Apple's audio brand.

name: Xilinx
description: Maker of programmable FPGA chips. AMD announced an all-stock acquisition in October 2020 and closed it on February 14, 2022. The Xilinx brand was retired in June 2023.

name: Los Angeles Clippers
description: Steve Ballmer bought the team for $2B in 2014, and Forbes values it at $7.5B. Since 2024–25 it has played in the privately financed, roughly $2B Intuit Dome in Inglewood, the first home venue the franchise has owned. In September 2026 the NBA fined it $30M, stripped five first-round picks and suspended Ballmer for a year over the Kawhi Leonard investigation, findings the team disputes. Tagged Movies & Entertainment, where listed sports franchises sit in GICS.

name: Ballmer Group
description: Founded in 2015 by Steve and Connie Ballmer and organized as an LLC rather than a private foundation. It funds economic mobility for children and families in southeast Michigan, Washington state and Los Angeles County, including $425M to the University of Oregon (2022) for a children's behavioral-health institute.

name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
description: Lisa Su earned her bachelor's, master's and PhD in electrical engineering here.

name: Bloomberg L.P.
description: Financial terminal, data and news company founded in 1981 as Innovative Market Systems. It is private, about 88% owned by Michael Bloomberg, and not on the Fortune 500 despite about $15B of revenue (2024).

name: Bloomberg Philanthropies
description: Michael Bloomberg's philanthropic organization. With the Gates Foundation it pledged $500M against tobacco use in 2008, and Bloomberg has committed his Bloomberg L.P. stake to it.

name: Salomon Brothers
description: Wall Street bond house where Michael Bloomberg was a partner. It merged with Phibro in 1981, and in 1987 Berkshire Hathaway bought $700M of its preferred stock to fend off Ronald Perelman. After the 1991 Treasury-auction scandal Warren Buffett briefly served as chairman. Travelers bought it in 1997, and it became part of Citigroup.

name: Merrill Lynch
description: Bloomberg's first terminal customer, which bought 30% of the company for $30M in 1982 and sold the last 20% back for about $4.4B in 2008. Bank of America acquired Merrill for about $50B in a deal announced in September 2008 and completed in January 2009.

name: Citadel
description: Ken Griffin's multistrategy hedge fund, founded in Chicago in 1990 with $4.6M and moved to Miami in 2022. It managed about $77B in 2026 and had about $90B of net gains since inception.

name: Citadel Securities
description: Market maker founded in 2002, involved in about one in four U.S. stock trades and the largest NYSE designated market maker. It earns much of its retail flow by paying brokers for orders. Sequoia and Paradigm invested $1.15B in 2022 at a $22B valuation.

name: Robinhood
description: Commission-free broker founded in 2013 by Stanford classmates Vlad Tenev and Baiju Bhatt. It went public in 2021 and joined the S&P 500 in 2025. Its revenue relies heavily on payment for order flow, with Citadel Securities its top venue. Its January 2021 GameStop trading limits led to congressional hearings at which Griffin also testified.

name: Melvin Capital
description: Gabe Plotkin's hedge fund (2014–2022). It lost 53% in January 2021 on GameStop shorts, and Citadel and Point72 injected $2.75B. It closed in 2022.

name: E*Trade
description: Online broker that took a $2.5B rescue from Citadel in November 2007, giving Citadel 19.99% and a board seat. Citadel exited in 2013. Morgan Stanley bought E*Trade for about $13B in October 2020.

name: Rocket Companies
description: Parent of Rocket Mortgage (formerly Quicken Loans), the largest U.S. mortgage lender. It went public in 2020 and is controlled by Dan Gilbert's Rock Holdings. It agreed to buy Redfin and Mr. Cooper in 2025. It ranked #619 on the 2025 Fortune 1000, outside the Fortune 500.

name: Intuit
description: Maker of TurboTax and QuickBooks. It bought Rock Financial for about $532M in stock in 1999, renamed it Quicken Loans, and sold it back to Dan Gilbert's group in 2002.

name: Cleveland Cavaliers
description: NBA franchise Dan Gilbert bought from Gordon Gund's group for $375M in 2005. It won the 2016 NBA title and plays in Rocket Arena.

name: Lennar
description: Miami homebuilder founded in 1954 by Leonard Miller and Arnold Rosen. It became the largest U.S. homebuilder after merging with CalAtlantic in 2018 and is controlled by Stuart Miller through ten-vote Class B shares.

name: University of Miami
description: Private research university in Coral Gables, Florida. Its Leonard M. Miller School of Medicine is named for Lennar's co-founder, and Stuart Miller chairs the UHealth board.

name: Koch, Inc.
description: Wichita conglomerate, renamed from Koch Industries in 2024. It is the second-largest U.S. private company (about $125B revenue) and is not on the Fortune 500 because it is private. It owns Georgia-Pacific, Molex, Guardian, Flint Hills Resources, Invista and Infor.

name: Georgia-Pacific
description: Atlanta maker of tissue, paper, packaging and building products. It was NYSE-listed as GP until Koch bought it for $21B in 2005, and it was a longtime Infor customer.

name: Molex
description: Maker of electronic, electrical and fiber-optic connectors, formerly Nasdaq-listed as MOLX. Koch bought it for $7.2B in 2013.

name: Infor
description: ERP software vendor that Koch bought in stages (two-thirds for $2.68B in 2017, the rest in 2020 at an $11B valuation). From 2010 to 2019 it was run by former Oracle co-president Charles Phillips, and in 2020 it ranked third in enterprise software behind Oracle and SAP. Its CloudSuite runs on Amazon Web Services.

name: Charlotte Hornets (Bobcats)
description: Founded as the Charlotte Bobcats when Robert L. Johnson's group was awarded the franchise in December 2002 for a $300M expansion fee. Michael Jordan bought control in 2010 for $275M and sold it in 2023 at about a $3B valuation to Gabe Plotkin and Rick Schnall.

name: Aftermath Entertainment
description: Dr. Dre's label, founded in 1996 after he left Death Row and distributed by Interscope. It signed Eminem, 50 Cent and Kendrick Lamar.

name: Death Row Records
description: Founded in 1991 by Dr. Dre and Suge Knight. Interscope took on its distribution in 1992, which put the label at the center of the mid-1990s fight over gangsta rap.

name: Interscope Records
description: Founded by Jimmy Iovine and Ted Field in 1989–90 as a $20M joint venture with Atlantic. Time Warner sold its half back in 1995 for $115M, and MCA bought 50% in 1996 for about $200M. In 1999 it merged with Geffen and A&M as Interscope Geffen A&M under Universal Music Group.

name: World Wide Technology
description: Founded in 1990 by David Steward and Jim Kavanaugh in the St. Louis area. It has about $20B in revenue and more than 14,000 employees, and it is the largest Black-owned company in the U.S. It is Cisco's largest global partner, Dell's first Titanium Black partner and an Elite Nvidia partner.

name: Cisco Systems
description: Networking company founded in 1984 by Stanford computer scientists, #83 on the 2025 Fortune 500. In March 2024 it closed its $28B purchase of Splunk.

name: Xerox
description: Founded in 1906 as the Haloid Photographic Company in Rochester; its Xerox 914 (1959) was the first plain-paper copier. Under Ursula Burns it bought ACS for $6.4B and, with Carl Icahn pressing for change, spun the services business off as Conduent in 2016–17. Ranked #565 by Fortune in 2025, outside the Fortune 500.

name: American Express
description: Founded in 1850 as a freight forwarder by Henry Wells, William Fargo and John Butterfield; it launched its charge card in 1958 and is #58 on the 2025 Fortune 500. It became a bank holding company in 2008, and Berkshire Hathaway is a major long-term holder.

name: Merck & Co.
description: Founded in 1891 as the U.S. arm of Germany's Merck; seized in 1917 and bought back in 1919 by George F. Merck. It bought Schering-Plough for $41B in 2009, which brought Keytruda, the drug behind nearly half its 2024 revenue. It is #65 on the 2025 Fortune 500.

name: ExxonMobil
description: The largest publicly traded U.S. oil and gas company and #8 on the 2025 Fortune 500. Its board has included Ken Frazier (from 2009; lead director from 2020) and Ursula Burns (from 2012).

name: General Catalyst
description: Venture firm whose bets include Airbnb, Stripe, Snap, Livongo and Oscar. Ken Chenault has been its chairman since 2018, and Ken Frazier has led its health assurance initiatives since 2021.

name: OneTen
description: Launched in December 2020 by Ken Chenault, Ken Frazier, Charles Phillips, Ginni Rometty and Kevin Sharer, with 37 CEOs, to hire and promote one million Black Americans without four-year degrees over 10 years.

name: The Walt Disney Company
description: Founded October 16, 1923 by Walt and Roy Disney and based in Burbank. Under Bob Iger it bought Pixar (2006), Marvel (2009), Lucasfilm (2012) and most of 21st Century Fox (2019). Josh D'Amaro became CEO in March 2026.

name: Capital Cities/ABC
description: Formed when Capital Cities, led by Tom Murphy, bought ABC for $3.5B in 1985. Berkshire Hathaway financed the deal for a 25% stake. Disney bought it in 1996 for about $19B, and Berkshire booked a $2.2B pre-tax gain on the deal.

name: Pixar
description: Computer-animation studio controlled by Steve Jobs (49.65%). Disney bought it in stock in 2006 for about $7.4B, making Jobs Disney's largest individual shareholder.

name: Marvel Entertainment
description: Comics publisher and film-franchise owner. Disney bought it for about $4B, completing the deal in December 2009.

name: Lucasfilm
description: George Lucas's Star Wars studio. Disney bought it for $4.05B on December 21, 2012.

name: 21st Century Fox
description: The Murdoch family's film and TV group. Disney bought most of it for $71.3B on March 20, 2019, after outbidding Comcast. The broadcast, news and sports assets were spun off as Fox Corporation.

name: Angel City FC
description: Los Angeles women's soccer club. In July 2024 Willow Bay and Bob Iger took a controlling stake at a $250M valuation.

name: Citigroup
description: Formed October 8, 1998 by merging Citicorp with Sandy Weill's Travelers Group, which grew out of his 1986 takeover of Commercial Credit. Jamie Dimon was Weill's lieutenant until November 1998.

name: Bank One
description: Chicago-based bank that brought in Jamie Dimon as CEO in 2000. It merged with JPMorgan Chase on July 1, 2004.

name: Haven
description: Not-for-profit health venture that Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway and JPMorgan Chase announced in January 2018 for their U.S. employees. It closed at the end of February 2021.

name: GE Capital
description: GE's lending and leasing arm. Under Jack Welch it grew to about 40% of company revenue. It was Penske Truck Leasing's partner from 1988 until GE exited in 2015–17.

name: NBCUniversal
description: NBC came to GE with RCA in 1986. GE formed NBCUniversal with Vivendi's Universal in 2004, and Comcast took 51% in 2011 and bought GE's last 49% for $16.7B in 2013.

name: Hyatt Roller Bearing Company
description: New Jersey bearing maker that Alfred Sloan ran from 1899. GM bought it for $13.5M in 1916, and it entered GM through United Motors in 1918.

name: Alfred P. Sloan Foundation
description: Founded in 1934 by GM's Alfred P. Sloan Jr. It had $2.2B in assets in 2024.

name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center
description: Combines Memorial Hospital (1884) and the Sloan-Kettering Institute, founded in 1945 with money from Alfred Sloan's foundation and GM stock from Charles Kettering. The two formally merged in 1980.

name: Kettering University
description: Formerly General Motors Institute in Flint, Michigan. Mary Barra earned her electrical engineering degree there in 1985.

name: Roc Nation
description: Founded by Jay-Z on April 1, 2008 as an entertainment company co-owned with Live Nation. It covers artist management, a record label, and Roc Nation Sports (2013).

name: Live Nation Entertainment
description: The largest concert promoter and owner of Ticketmaster. It co-owns Roc Nation and backed its 2008 launch.

name: Tidal
description: Norwegian-Swedish streaming service bought by Jay-Z's company (as Aspiro) for about $56M in 2015 and relaunched with artist co-owners. Square (Block) bought a majority for $297M in 2021.

name: Armand de Brignac
description: The 'Ace of Spades' champagne, produced by the Cattier family. Jay-Z bought it in 2014, and LVMH acquired 50% in 2021.

name: Def Jam Recordings
description: Hip-hop label that distributed Roc-A-Fella from 1997. Jay-Z was its president from 2004 to 2007 and signed Rihanna there. It is part of Universal Music Group.

name: BET (Black Entertainment Television)
description: Founded by Robert and Sheila Johnson with $500K from John Malone and launched January 25, 1980. It listed on the NYSE in 1991, went private in 1998 and was sold to Viacom for about $3B (closed 2001). BET+ was a 2019 joint venture with Tyler Perry Studios.

name: RLJ Lodging Trust
description: Grew out of RLJ Development, which Robert L. Johnson founded in 2000, and went public in 2011. It owns about 100 premium-branded, focused-service and compact full-service hotels.

name: Harpo Productions
description: Oprah Winfrey's production company, founded in 1986. It took ownership of The Oprah Winfrey Show in 1988 and holds 5% of OWN.

name: Oprah Winfrey Network (OWN)
description: Joint venture of Discovery and Harpo that launched January 1, 2011 in place of Discovery Health. Discovery took about 74% in 2017 and 95% in 2020. Tyler Perry's scripted shows turned it around.

name: Tyler Perry Studios
description: 330-acre studio on the former Fort McPherson army base in Atlanta, bought in 2015 and opened in 2019 with 12 soundstages. Tyler Perry owns it outright.

name: Fenty Beauty
description: Launched September 8, 2017 by Rihanna through LVMH's Kendo incubator and owned 50/50 by Rihanna and LVMH. It is sold through Sephora and Ulta.

name: Savage X Fenty
description: Founded in May 2018 by Rihanna with TechStyle Fashion Group. It was valued at $1B in 2021.

name: Magic Johnson Enterprises
description: Founded in 1987 in Beverly Hills. Its ventures include Loews theaters (1995), Starbucks' Urban Coffee Opportunities (1998–2010), Canyon-Johnson Urban Funds (2001), the Dodgers (2012) and EquiTrust (2015).

name: EquiTrust Life Insurance
description: Magic Johnson Enterprises bought a controlling interest in June 2015. Its assets grew from $16B to $33B (Forbes).

name: Los Angeles Dodgers
description: Bought from Frank McCourt in 2012 for $2.15B by Guggenheim Baseball Management (Mark Walter, Magic Johnson, Peter Guber, Stan Kasten, Todd Boehly, Bobby Patton).
